import Lax263307.ComputedSeparators
import Lax263307.ComputedRounding
import Lax263307.HeavyRationalConditioning
import Lax263307.AlgorithmParameters

/-!
---
title: Computed rounding oracle near the moment relaxation
type: theorem
---
The algorithm searches for a heavy conditioning set, computes separators
using the registered flow-cut solver, and queries the resulting parts.
Its actual output is either an independent set or a valid component cut
with a uniform gap and a bounded coefficient sum.

# Formalization notes

The child-query hypothesis is the induction hypothesis for the recursive
algorithm. All selections in the oracle are computable. Its implementation
and execution bounds in the registered RAM model are separate obligations.
-/

namespace Lax263307.NearOracle

open scoped NNRat
open LinearRelaxation RationalConditioning

def costs {n r : ℕ} (y : RationalVector n r) (A : Finset (Fin n)) (v : Fin n) : ℚ≥0 :=
  ⟨max 0 (rationalValue y (insert v A) / rationalValue y A), le_max_left _ _⟩

def order (q : ℕ) : List (Option (Fin q)) := none :: (List.finRange q).map some

inductive Result (n : ℕ)
  | found (vertices : Finset (Fin n))
  | cut (conditioning vertices : Finset (Fin n)) (bound : ℕ)
  | reject

def run {n : ℕ} (flow : List ℕ → List ℕ) (a K B D : ℕ)
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (k : ℕ)
    (y : RationalVector n (AlgorithmParameters.level a K B n D))
    (child : Finset (Fin n) → ℕ → Option (Finset (Fin n))) : Result n :=
  let p := AlgorithmParameters.sparsity a K B n D
  match HeavyRationalConditioning.findHeavyConditioning G k p y with
  | none => .reject
  | some A =>
    let x := costs y A
    let cs := ComputedSeparators.cuts
      (ComputedSeparators.step flow G x B (AlgorithmParameters.load B n D) k) n Finset.univ
    let parts := ComputedSeparators.pieces cs
    let c : Option (Fin cs.length) → ℚ := fun i => ∑ v ∈ parts i, (x v : ℚ)
    match ComputedRounding.collect (order cs.length) parts (1 / D) k c
      (fun i t => child (parts i) t) with
    | .found I => .found I
    | .cut C u => .cut A C u

def ChildCorrect {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (D h : ℕ)
    (child : Finset (Fin n) → ℕ → Option (Finset (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ∀ C : Finset (Fin n), 3 * C.card ≤ 2 * n → ∀ t : ℕ,
    match child C t with
    | some I => I ⊆ C ∧ G.IsIndepSet (I : Set (Fin n)) ∧
        (1 - 4 * (1 / (D : ℝ))) ^ h * (t : ℝ) ≤ I.card
    | none => IsIndependenceBound G C (t - 1)

def Correct {n r : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (k h D : ℕ) (η : ℝ)
    (x : MomentVector n r) : Result n → Prop
  | .found I => G.IsIndepSet (I : Set (Fin n)) ∧
      (1 - 4 * (1 / (D : ℝ))) ^ (h + 1) * (k : ℝ) ≤ I.card
  | .cut A C u => A.card ≤ r ∧ u ≤ n ∧ IsIndependenceBound G C u ∧
      (∀ z ∈ independentSetHull G k r,
        ComponentCutEncoding.evaluate (ComponentCutEncoding.coefficient A C u) z ≤ 0) ∧
      η * (1 / (D : ℝ)) ^ 2 / (16 * n) ≤
        ComponentCutEncoding.evaluate (ComponentCutEncoding.coefficient A C u) x ∧
      (∑ T : Coordinate n r, |(ComponentCutEncoding.coefficient A C u T : ℝ)|) ≤ 2 * n
  | .reject => False

open GraphClasses PowerBagBounds AlgorithmParameters

axiom exists_oracle (C : GraphClass) (hereditary : IsHereditary C)
    (a A : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) (hA : 0 < A) (class_bound : HasPowerBagBound C a A) :
    ∃ (flow : List ℕ → List ℕ) (K B : ℕ), Lax759944.RamPolytime.RamPolytime flow ∧
      0 < K ∧ 0 < B ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      G ∈ C n → 0 < n → ∀ (D k h : ℕ), 4 ≤ D → cutoff a K B n D < k →
      ∀ (y : RationalVector n (level a K B n D)),
      IsFeasible G k (level a K B n D) (realVector y) →
      ∀ (x : MomentVector n (level a K B n D)),
      (∀ T, |x T - realVector y T| ≤ (momentFloor a K B n D : ℝ) *
        (1 / (D : ℝ)) ^ 2 / (32 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2)) →
      ∀ (child : Finset (Fin n) → ℕ → Option (Finset (Fin n))), ChildCorrect G D h child →
      Correct G k h D (momentFloor a K B n D) x (run flow a K B D G k y child)

end Lax263307.NearOracle

concepts.title: Sparse bounded-load route distributions are impossible
concepts.description:
Suppose a hereditary class has a uniform power bound on decomposition bags.
There is a fixed positive integer $K$ such that a class member cannot support
a uniform-endpoint route distribution with vertex loads at most
$\ell x_v/k$, costs in $[0,1]$ of total mass at most $k$, and edge cost at
most $k^2/p$, when $k\ge K(\ell+1)^{4a+2}$ and
$p\ge2K(\ell+1)^{4a+2}$.

The registered source family supplies a graph large enough to contradict
the sampled width upper bound, while its size overshoot keeps its edge count
within the probability budgets.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The power bag bound is an explicit hypothesis. Deriving it from strongly
edge-sublinear separators is a remaining part of the main proof. No source
graph construction is needed by the separator algorithm: this family is
used only in the contradiction that rules out its high-flow branch.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown:
Bonnet–Chang, the sampled-path contradiction of Lemma 11, with the registered
subcubic source family from Lax920634.

concepts.title: Collision and length bounds for independently sampled paths
concepts.description:
Let $Q$ be a random vertex set and let $q_v=\Pr[v\in Q]$. Two independent
samples intersect with probability at most $\sum_v q_v^2$. The probability
that an edge joins their vertex sets is at most the ordered adjacency mass
$\sum_{uv\in E(G)}2q_uq_v$. Also $\mathbb E[|Q|]=\sum_vq_v$.

Consequently, if $q_v\le\ell x_v/k$, $0\le x_v\le1$, $\sum_vx_v\le k$ with $k>0$,
and $e_G(x)\le k^2/p$ with $p>0$, these bounds are respectively
$\ell^2/k$, $2\ell^2/p$, and $\ell$.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
A finite distribution is given explicitly by its outcome probabilities.
The pair probabilities are products, expressing independent sampling.
The estimates depend only on the vertex sets of the sampled paths, so the
definitions allow arbitrary finite vertex sets.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown: Bonnet–Chang, equations (8), (9), and the expected-path-size bound in Lemma 11.

import Lax263307.Entropy
import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Card

/-!
---
title: Collision and length bounds for independently sampled paths
type: theorem
---
Let $Q$ be a random vertex set and let $q_v=\Pr[v\in Q]$. Two independent
samples intersect with probability at most $\sum_v q_v^2$. The probability
that an edge joins their vertex sets is at most the ordered adjacency mass
$\sum_{uv\in E(G)}2q_uq_v$. Also $\mathbb E[|Q|]=\sum_vq_v$.

Consequently, if $q_v\le\ell x_v/k$, $0\le x_v\le1$, $\sum_vx_v\le k$ with $k>0$,
and $e_G(x)\le k^2/p$ with $p>0$, these bounds are respectively
$\ell^2/k$, $2\ell^2/p$, and $\ell$.

# Formalization notes

A finite distribution is given explicitly by its outcome probabilities.
The pair probabilities are products, expressing independent sampling.
The estimates depend only on the vertex sets of the sampled paths, so the
definitions allow arbitrary finite vertex sets.

# Attribution

Bonnet–Chang, equations (8), (9), and the expected-path-size bound in Lemma 11.
-/

namespace Lax263307.PathSampling

/-- Finite outcome probabilities and their associated vertex sets. -/
structure Distribution (n q : ℕ) where
  /-- Probability of each outcome. -/
  probability : Fin q → ℝ
  /-- Probabilities are nonnegative. -/
  nonnegative : ∀ i, 0 ≤ probability i
  /-- Total probability is one. -/
  normalized : (∑ i, probability i) = 1
  /-- The vertices used by each outcome. -/
  vertices : Fin q → Finset (Fin n)

/-- Probability of using a particular vertex. -/
noncomputable def load {n q : ℕ} (P : Distribution n q) (v : Fin n) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, if v ∈ P.vertices i then P.probability i else 0

/-- Expected number of used vertices. -/
noncomputable def expectedSize {n q : ℕ} (P : Distribution n q) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, P.probability i * ((P.vertices i).card : ℝ)

/-- Probability that independent outcomes have a common vertex. -/
noncomputable def collisionProbability {n q : ℕ} (P : Distribution n q) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, ∑ j, if ¬Disjoint (P.vertices i) (P.vertices j) then
    P.probability i * P.probability j else 0

/-- Probability that a graph edge joins independent outcomes. -/
noncomputable def adjacencyProbability {n q : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (P : Distribution n q) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, ∑ j, if ∃ u ∈ P.vertices i, ∃ v ∈ P.vertices j, G.Adj u v then
    P.probability i * P.probability j else 0

/-- Sum of vertex-use probabilities equals expected size. -/
axiom expected_size_identity {n q : ℕ} (P : Distribution n q) :
  expectedSize P = ∑ v, load P v

/-- The union bound for intersection of two independent samples. -/
axiom collision_union_bound {n q : ℕ} (P : Distribution n q) :
  collisionProbability P ≤ ∑ v, (load P v) ^ 2

/-- The union bound for edges joining two independent samples. -/
axiom adjacency_union_bound {n q : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (P : Distribution n q) :
  adjacencyProbability G P ≤ Entropy.adjacencyMass G (load P)

/-- The load hypotheses imply the three estimates used in sampling. -/
axiom sampling_bounds {n q : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (P : Distribution n q) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (k ℓ p : ℝ)
    (k_positive : 0 < k) (ℓ_nonnegative : 0 ≤ ℓ) (p_positive : 0 < p)
    (cost_bounds : ∀ v, 0 ≤ x v ∧ x v ≤ 1) (mass : (∑ v, x v) ≤ k)
    (load_bound : ∀ v, load P v ≤ ℓ * x v / k)
    (edge_bound : Entropy.edgeCost G x ≤ k ^ 2 / p) :
    collisionProbability P ≤ ℓ ^ 2 / k ∧

concepts.title: Removing nonpositive weights
concepts.description:
Replace each rational weight $w_v$ by $\max(w_v,0)$. An approximation for
these nonnegative weights yields the same approximation for the original
weights by removing the nonpositive-weight vertices of its returned set.
If all weights are nonpositive, the empty set is optimal.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Clipping changes only vertex weights, so the graph stays in its original
class. Removing selected vertices preserves independence. The approximation
transfer assumes an accuracy in $[0,1]$.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.WeightedIndependentSet

/-!
---
title: Removing nonpositive weights
type: theorem
---
Replace each rational weight $w_v$ by $\max(w_v,0)$. An approximation for
these nonnegative weights yields the same approximation for the original
weights by removing the nonpositive-weight vertices of its returned set.
If all weights are nonpositive, the empty set is optimal.

# Formalization notes

Clipping changes only vertex weights, so the graph stays in its original
class. Removing selected vertices preserves independence. The approximation
transfer assumes an accuracy in $[0,1]$.
-/

namespace Lax263307.PositiveWeights

open WeightedIndependentSet

/-- Clip negative weights to zero. -/
def positiveWeights {n : ℕ} (w : Fin n → ℚ) : Fin n → ℚ := fun v => max (w v) 0

/-- Retain only the strictly positive-weight vertices of a returned set. -/
def discardNonpositive {n : ℕ} (w : Fin n → ℚ) (I : Finset (Fin n)) : Finset (Fin n) :=
  I.filter fun v => 0 < w v

/-- Approximation for clipped weights transfers to arbitrary signed weights. -/
axiom signed_weight_transfer {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (w : Fin n → ℚ)
    (ε : ℚ) (accuracy_nonnegative : 0 ≤ ε) (accuracy_le_one : ε ≤ 1)
    (I : Finset (Fin n)) (approximation : IsApproximation G (positiveWeights w) ε I) :
    IsApproximation G w ε (discardNonpositive w I)

/-- The empty set solves instances whose weights are all nonpositive. -/
axiom nonpositive_case {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (w : Fin n → ℚ)
    (nonpositive : ∀ v, w v ≤ 0) (ε : ℚ) (accuracy_nonnegative : 0 ≤ ε)
    (accuracy_le_one : ε ≤ 1) : IsApproximation G w ε ∅

end Lax263307.PositiveWeights

      Rat.instLE.le 0 ε →
        Rat.instLE.le ε 1 →
          Lax263307.WeightedIndependentSet.IsApproximation G w ε Finset.instEmptyCollection.emptyCollection

concepts.title: Integer power bounds on class decomposition bags
concepts.description:
A uniform bound $|B|^a\le A(m+1)^{a-1}$ gives the monotone bag-size function
$W(m)=\lfloor\sqrt[a]{A(m+1)^{a-1}}\rfloor$. For $a,A>0$, this function
is at least one and obeys the same power bound. Integer powers suffice for
the sampled width contradiction once separators yield such a class bound.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown: An integer form of the sublinear width bound used in Bonnet–Chang's Lemma 11.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.InducedEmbeddingWidth
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.NthRootLemmas

/-!
---
title: Integer power bounds on class decomposition bags
type: theorem
---
A uniform bound $|B|^a\le A(m+1)^{a-1}$ gives the monotone bag-size function
$W(m)=\lfloor\sqrt[a]{A(m+1)^{a-1}}\rfloor$. For $a,A>0$, this function
is at least one and obeys the same power bound. Integer powers suffice for
the sampled width contradiction once separators yield such a class bound.

# Attribution

An integer form of the sublinear width bound used in Bonnet–Chang's Lemma 11.
-/

namespace Lax263307.PowerBagBounds

open Lax263307.GraphClasses Lax263307.InducedEmbeddingWidth Lax228581.Treewidth

def HasPowerBagBound (C : GraphClass) (a A : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ n (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G ∈ C n → ∃ D : TreeDecomposition G,
    ∀ i, (D.bag i).card ^ a ≤ A * (G.edgeSet.ncard + 1) ^ (a - 1)

def bagBound (a A m : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.nthRoot a (A * (m + 1) ^ (a - 1))

axiom root_bag_bound (C : GraphClass) (a A : ℕ) (a_positive : 0 < a) (A_positive : 0 < A)
    (class_bound : HasPowerBagBound C a A) :
    Monotone (bagBound a A) ∧ HasBagBound C (bagBound a A) ∧
      (∀ m, 1 ≤ bagBound a A m) ∧
      (∀ m, (bagBound a A m) ^ a ≤ A * (m + 1) ^ (a - 1))

end Lax263307.PowerBagBounds

root_bag_bound : ∀ (C : Lax263307.GraphClasses.GraphClass) (a A : Nat),
  instLTNat.lt 0 a →
    instLTNat.lt 0 A →
      Lax263307.PowerBagBounds.HasPowerBagBound C a A →
        And (Monotone (Lax263307.PowerBagBounds.bagBound a A))
          (And (Lax263307.InducedEmbeddingWidth.HasBagBound C (Lax263307.PowerBagBounds.bagBound a A))
            (And (∀ (m : Nat), instLENat.le 1 (Lax263307.PowerBagBounds.bagBound a A m))
              (∀ (m : Nat),
                instLENat.le (instHPow.hPow (Lax263307.PowerBagBounds.bagBound a A m) a)
                  (instHMul.hMul A (instHPow.hPow (instHAdd.hAdd m 1) (instHSub.hSub a 1))))))

concepts.title: The bounded projected round-or-cut search
concepts.description:
The actual registered LP certificate decides whether to reject, separate
by a projection cut, or call the computed near-relaxation oracle.
Both cut branches preserve the same explicit dyadic cube about every
scaled independent-set encoding. The bounded rounded ellipsoid loop
therefore returns an approximate independent set or a valid upper bound
strictly below the requested positive target.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The only recursive hypothesis concerns answers on balanced child parts.
The LP and flow functions are fixed for the class and have the registered
RAM polynomial-time guarantees. The surrounding computable search still
needs its own finite RAM implementation and time bound.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.NearOracle
import Lax263307.RegisteredLP
import Lax263307.RationalProjection
import Lax263307.RationalCutBuffer

/-!
---
title: The bounded projected round-or-cut search
type: theorem
---
The actual registered LP certificate decides whether to reject, separate
by a projection cut, or call the computed near-relaxation oracle.
Both cut branches preserve the same explicit dyadic cube about every
scaled independent-set encoding. The bounded rounded ellipsoid loop
therefore returns an approximate independent set or a valid upper bound
strictly below the requested positive target.

# Formalization notes

The only recursive hypothesis concerns answers on balanced child parts.
The LP and flow functions are fixed for the class and have the registered
RAM polynomial-time guarantees. The surrounding computable search still
needs its own finite RAM implementation and time bound.
-/

namespace Lax263307.ProjectedOracle

open LinearRelaxation AlgorithmParameters

def tolerance (a K B n D : ℕ) : ℚ := momentFloor a K B n D / (32 * (n : ℚ)^2 * (D : ℚ)^2)

def raw {N : ℕ} (center : Fin N → ℚ) : Fin N → ℚ := fun i => 4 * (N : ℚ) * center i

def run {n : ℕ} (lp flow : List ℕ → List ℕ) (a K B D : ℕ)
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (k : ℕ)
    (child : Finset (Fin n) → ℕ → Option (Finset (Fin n)))
    (center : MomentLP.Index n (level a K B n D) → ℚ) :
    RoundedOracleSearch.Reply (MomentLP.dimension n (level a K B n D)) (Finset (Fin n)) :=
  let P := MomentLP.program G k (level a K B n D)
  match RationalProjection.classify P (tolerance a K B n D)
    (RegisteredLP.certificate lp (DistanceProjection.distanceProgram P (raw center))) with
  | .reject => .reject
  | .far normal _ => .cut (RationalCutBuffer.integerNormal normal)
  | .near y =>
    match NearOracle.run flow a K B D G k (MomentLP.decode y) child with
    | .reject => .reject
    | .found I => .found I
    | .cut A C u => .cut (RationalCutBuffer.integerNormal
        (RoundedOracleSearch.rationalNormal (MomentLP.encode (ComponentCutEncoding.coefficient A C u))))

def Good {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (k h D : ℕ) (I : Finset (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  G.IsIndepSet (I : Set (Fin n)) ∧ (1 - 4 * (1 / (D : ℝ))) ^ (h+1) * (k : ℝ) ≤ I.card

def Correct {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (k h a K B D : ℕ)
    (center : MomentLP.Index n (level a K B n D) → ℚ) :
    RoundedOracleSearch.Reply (MomentLP.dimension n (level a K B n D)) (Finset (Fin n)) → Prop
  | .found I => Good G k h D I
  | .reject => independentSetHull G k (level a K B n D) = ∅
  | .cut normal => (∃ i, normal i ≠ 0) ∧
    ∀ z ∈ independentSetHull G k (level a K B n D),
    ∀ e : MomentLP.Index n (level a K B n D) → ℝ,
    (∀ i, |e i| ≤ ((2 : ℝ) ^ precision a K B n D)⁻¹) →
      (fun i => (normal i : ℝ)) ⬝ᵥ
        (BufferedEllipsoid.scale (MomentLP.encode z) + e - (fun i => (center i : ℝ))) ≤ 0

def search {n : ℕ} (lp flow : List ℕ → List ℕ) (a K B D : ℕ)
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (k : ℕ)
    (child : Finset (Fin n) → ℕ → Option (Finset (Fin n))) : Option (Finset (Fin n)) :=
  RoundedOracleSearch.search (fun _ center => run lp flow a K B D G k child center)
    (precision a K B n D)

def SearchCorrect {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (k h D : ℕ) : Option (Finset (Fin n)) → Prop
  | some I => Good G k h D I
  | none => IsIndependenceBound G Finset.univ (k-1)

open GraphClasses PowerBagBounds

axiom exists_search (C : GraphClass) (hereditary : IsHereditary C)
    (a A : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) (hA : 0 < A) (class_bound : HasPowerBagBound C a A) :
    ∃ (lp flow : List ℕ → List ℕ) (K B : ℕ),
      Lax759944.RamPolytime.RamPolytime lp ∧ Lax759944.RamPolytime.RamPolytime flow ∧
      0 < K ∧ 0 < B ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      G ∈ C n → 0 < n → ∀ (D k h : ℕ), 4 ≤ D → cutoff a K B n D < k →
      ∀ (child : Finset (Fin n) → ℕ → Option (Finset (Fin n))),
      Lax263307.NearOracle.ChildCorrect G D h child →
      SearchCorrect G k h D (search lp flow a K B D G k child)

end Lax263307.ProjectedOracle

  Lax263307.GraphClasses.IsHereditary C →
    ∀ (a A : Nat),
      instLTNat.lt 0 a →
        instLTNat.lt 0 A →
          Lax263307.PowerBagBounds.HasPowerBagBound C a A →
            Exists fun lp =>
              Exists fun flow =>
                Exists fun K =>
                  Exists fun B =>
                    And (Lax759944.RamPolytime.RamPolytime lp)
                      (And (Lax759944.RamPolytime.RamPolytime flow)
                        (And (instLTNat.lt 0 K)

                              Set.instMembership.mem (C n) G →
                                instLTNat.lt 0 n →
                                  ∀ (D k h : Nat),
                                    instLENat.le 4 D →
                                      instLTNat.lt (Lax263307.AlgorithmParameters.cutoff a K B n D) k →
                                        ∀ (child : Finset (Fin n) → Nat → Option (Finset (Fin n))),

                                            Lax263307.ProjectedOracle.SearchCorrect G k h D

concepts.title: Deterministic quasipolynomial-time approximation schemes
concepts.description:
A deterministic QPTAS for maximum-weight independent set on a class
$\mathcal C$ uses one finite program, depending only on $\mathcal C$,
which returns a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation on every member with
rational weights and rational $0<\varepsilon<1$.
Its running time has the form
$$2^{(\varepsilon^{-1}\log(n+2))^{O_{\mathcal C}(1)}}
  +(\ell+1)^{O_{\mathcal C}(1)},$$
where $\ell$ is the binary length of the weights and accuracy.
Neither class recognition nor a separator is supplied as input.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Execution is `Lax808846.Ram.RunsTo` on the registered word RAM.
The supplied input is exactly `encodeInput`, with no implicit length prefix.
The constants and program precede the input and word width in the quantifiers.
The natural-number time bound uses $\lceil1/\varepsilon\rceil$ and
$1+\lfloor\log_2(n+2)\rfloor$ to cover small inputs.

The same bound is a sufficient word width, and the program must work at
every larger width. In particular it works at that explicitly prescribed
width; there is no advice hidden in a choice of width. Allowing this many
bits accommodates exact rational subroutines. Simulating these bounded-word
operations with bit operations costs a polynomial in the time bound,
which remains of the displayed form after increasing its constants and
exponent: $(A+B)^k\le2^{k-1}(A^k+B^k)$. Thus the additive polynomial
dependence on $\ell$ is preserved. Correctness and time are promised only
on well-formed inputs whose graphs belong to $\mathcal C$.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.GraphClasses
import Lax263307.WeightedIndependentSet
import Lax808846.Ram
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Log

/-!
---
title: Deterministic quasipolynomial-time approximation schemes
type: definition
---
A deterministic QPTAS for maximum-weight independent set on a class
$\mathcal C$ uses one finite program, depending only on $\mathcal C$,
which returns a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation on every member with
rational weights and rational $0<\varepsilon<1$.
Its running time has the form
$$2^{(\varepsilon^{-1}\log(n+2))^{O_{\mathcal C}(1)}}
  +(\ell+1)^{O_{\mathcal C}(1)},$$
where $\ell$ is the binary length of the weights and accuracy.
Neither class recognition nor a separator is supplied as input.

# Formalization notes

Execution is `Lax808846.Ram.RunsTo` on the registered word RAM.
The supplied input is exactly `encodeInput`, with no implicit length prefix.
The constants and program precede the input and word width in the quantifiers.
The natural-number time bound uses $\lceil1/\varepsilon\rceil$ and
$1+\lfloor\log_2(n+2)\rfloor$ to cover small inputs.

The same bound is a sufficient word width, and the program must work at
every larger width. In particular it works at that explicitly prescribed
width; there is no advice hidden in a choice of width. Allowing this many
bits accommodates exact rational subroutines. Simulating these bounded-word
operations with bit operations costs a polynomial in the time bound,
which remains of the displayed form after increasing its constants and
exponent: $(A+B)^k\le2^{k-1}(A^k+B^k)$. Thus the additive polynomial
dependence on $\ell$ is preserved. Correctness and time are promised only
on well-formed inputs whose graphs belong to $\mathcal C$.
-/

namespace Lax263307.QPTAS

open GraphClasses WeightedIndependentSet Lax808846.Ram

/-- An explicit bound representing the paper's two-parameter running time. -/
def timeBound (c d n ℓ : ℕ) (ε : ℚ) : ℕ :=
  2 ^ (c * (⌈ε⁻¹⌉₊ * (Nat.log2 (n + 2) + 1)) ^ d) + c * (ℓ + 1) ^ d

/-- One uniform deterministic word-RAM program realizes the approximation scheme. -/
def HasQPTAS (C : GraphClass) : Prop :=
  ∃ (program : Program) (c d : ℕ), 0 < c ∧ 0 < d ∧
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      G ∈ C n → ∀ (weights : Fin n → ℚ) (ε : ℚ), 0 < ε → ε < 1 →
        let T := timeBound c d n (rationalBitSize weights ε) ε
        ∀ wordLength : ℕ, T ≤ wordLength →
          ∃ I : Finset (Fin n), IsApproximation G weights ε I ∧
            ∃ t ≤ T, RunsTo wordLength program
              (encodeInput G weights ε) (encodeOutput I) t

end Lax263307.QPTAS

concepts.title: Exact rational search for a conditioning set
concepts.description:
For a rational feasible point of $R_r(G,k)$, enumerate the vertex sets
of size at most $r$ and return the first set $A$ satisfying $y_A>0$ and
$$p\sum_{u,v:\,uv\in E(G)}y_{A\cup\{u\}}y_{A\cup\{v\}}
  \le2k^2y_A^2.$$
The sum counts ordered adjacent pairs. This exact rational test is equivalent
to the edge-cost condition in Lemma 12. Under that lemma's hypotheses the
search succeeds and returns the required costs. The list contains at most
$(r+1)(n+1)^r$ candidates.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Candidates are generated as sublists of each prescribed length, in a fixed
order. Enumeration does not first materialize the full power set.
This statement proves exact search correctness and bounds its candidate count;
the RAM instruction and bit-length bounds are separate obligations.

import Lax263307.ConditioningExistence
import Mathlib.Data.Rat.Cast.Order
import Mathlib.Data.List.Sublists
import Mathlib.Data.List.FinRange
import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Card

/-!
---
title: Exact rational search for a conditioning set
type: theorem
---
For a rational feasible point of $R_r(G,k)$, enumerate the vertex sets
of size at most $r$ and return the first set $A$ satisfying $y_A>0$ and
$$p\sum_{u,v:\,uv\in E(G)}y_{A\cup\{u\}}y_{A\cup\{v\}}
  \le2k^2y_A^2.$$
The sum counts ordered adjacent pairs. This exact rational test is equivalent
to the edge-cost condition in Lemma 12. Under that lemma's hypotheses the
search succeeds and returns the required costs. The list contains at most
$(r+1)(n+1)^r$ candidates.

# Formalization notes

Candidates are generated as sublists of each prescribed length, in a fixed
order. Enumeration does not first materialize the full power set.
This statement proves exact search correctness and bounds its candidate count;
the RAM instruction and bit-length bounds are separate obligations.
-/

namespace Lax263307.RationalConditioning

open LinearRelaxation Entropy

/-- Rational coordinates for the same truncated relaxation. -/
abbrev RationalVector (n r : ℕ) := Coordinate n r → ℚ

/-- Interpret a rational moment vector in the real vector space. -/
def realVector {n r : ℕ} (y : RationalVector n r) : MomentVector n r :=
  fun A => (y A : ℝ)

/-- Read a rational coordinate, extending by zero outside the coordinate domain. -/
def rationalValue {n r : ℕ} (y : RationalVector n r) (A : Finset (Fin n)) : ℚ :=
  if h : A.card ≤ r + 2 then y ⟨A, h⟩ else 0

/-- The ordered edge-product numerator in the exact test. -/
def edgeNumerator {n r : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (y : RationalVector n r) (A : Finset (Fin n)) : ℚ :=
  ∑ u, ∑ v, if G.Adj u v then
    rationalValue y (insert u A) * rationalValue y (insert v A) else 0

/-- The exact rational test after clearing the positive conditioning denominator. -/
def Passes {n r : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (k p : ℕ) (y : RationalVector n r) (A : Finset (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  0 < rationalValue y A ∧
    (p : ℚ) * edgeNumerator G y A ≤ 2 * (k : ℚ) ^ 2 * rationalValue y A ^ 2

/-- The rational test is decidable by exact arithmetic. -/
instance {n r : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (k p : ℕ) (y : RationalVector n r) (A : Finset (Fin n)) : Decidable (Passes G k p y A) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (0 < rationalValue y A ∧
    (p : ℚ) * edgeNumerator G y A ≤ 2 * (k : ℚ) ^ 2 * rationalValue y A ^ 2))

/-- Enumerate only sublists with lengths between zero and the conditioning budget. -/
def candidates (n r : ℕ) : List (Finset (Fin n)) :=
  (List.range (r + 1)).flatMap fun j =>
    ((List.finRange n).sublistsLen j).map List.toFinset

/-- Return the first candidate satisfying the rational test. -/
def findConditioning {n r : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (k p : ℕ) (y : RationalVector n r) : Option (Finset (Fin n)) :=
  (candidates n r).find? fun A => decide (Passes G k p y A)

/-- The candidate list contains exactly the vertex sets within the budget. -/
axiom candidate_complete (n r : ℕ) (A : Finset (Fin n)) :
  A ∈ candidates n r ↔ A.card ≤ r

/-- The number of candidates has the required polynomial dependence on `n` at fixed `r`. -/
axiom candidate_bound (n r : ℕ) : (candidates n r).length ≤ (r + 1) * (n + 1) ^ r

/-- The exact rational search returns a conditioning set with the promised costs. -/
axiom search_correct {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (k r p : ℕ) (y : RationalVector n r) (feasible : IsFeasible G k r (realVector y))
    (target_positive : 0 < k) (level_positive : 0 < r) (threshold_positive : 0 < p)
    (budget : 2 * (p : ℝ) * Real.logb 2 n ≤ r) :
    ∃ A : Finset (Fin n), findConditioning G k p y = some A ∧ A.card ≤ r ∧
      0 < value (realVector y) A ∧
      (∀ v, 0 ≤ conditioned (realVector y) A v ∧ conditioned (realVector y) A v ≤ 1) ∧
      (∑ v, conditioned (realVector y) A v) = k ∧
      edgeCost G (conditioned (realVector y) A) ≤ (k : ℝ) ^ 2 / p

end Lax263307.RationalConditioning

concepts.title: Rational cut normals preserve protected cubes after scaling
concepts.description:
Clear all rational normal coefficients by one positive product of denominators.
The resulting integer normal defines the same central half-space. Its bit size
is bounded by the numerator bit size plus the sum of denominator bit sizes.
A positive query gap, together with a bound on the sum of absolute coefficients,
protects a whole coordinate cube about every valid point. Scaling coordinates
by 4N and clearing denominators preserve that protected central cut.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Both clearing operations are computable. Only the correctness argument uses
real casts. The scaled-cube guarantee supplies the cut hypothesis for the
actual rounded ellipsoid loop; it does not assume that the exact hull has
interior. The numerator calculation matches the registered LP size-bound
construction and is proved directly from divisibility of the denominator
product.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.BufferedEllipsoid
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Size

/-!
---
title: Rational cut normals preserve protected cubes after scaling
type: theorem
---
Clear all rational normal coefficients by one positive product of denominators.
The resulting integer normal defines the same central half-space. Its bit size
is bounded by the numerator bit size plus the sum of denominator bit sizes.
A positive query gap, together with a bound on the sum of absolute coefficients,
protects a whole coordinate cube about every valid point. Scaling coordinates
by 4N and clearing denominators preserve that protected central cut.

# Formalization notes

Both clearing operations are computable. Only the correctness argument uses
real casts. The scaled-cube guarantee supplies the cut hypothesis for the
actual rounded ellipsoid loop; it does not assume that the exact hull has
interior. The numerator calculation matches the registered LP size-bound
construction and is proved directly from divisibility of the denominator
product.
-/

namespace Lax263307.RationalCutBuffer

open Matrix

def denominator {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n → ℚ) : ℕ := ∏ i, (a i).den

def integerNormal {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n → ℚ) (i : Fin n) : ℤ :=
  (a i).num * (denominator a / (a i).den : ℕ)

axiom denominator_positive {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n → ℚ) : 0 < denominator a

axiom integer_normal_cast {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n → ℚ) (i : Fin n) :
    (integerNormal a i : ℝ) = (denominator a : ℝ) * (a i : ℝ)

axiom normal_nonzero {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n → ℚ) (x z : Fin n → ℝ)
    (gap : (fun i => (a i : ℝ)) ⬝ᵥ z < (fun i => (a i : ℝ)) ⬝ᵥ x) :
    ∃ i, integerNormal a i ≠ 0

axiom denominator_bound {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n → ℚ) :
    denominator a ≤ 2 ^ (∑ i, Nat.size (a i).den)

axiom normal_size {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n → ℚ) (i : Fin n) :
    Nat.size (integerNormal a i).natAbs ≤
      Nat.size (a i).num.natAbs + ∑ j, Nat.size (a j).den

axiom dot_stable {n : ℕ} (a x y : Fin n → ℝ) (ρ L : ℝ)
    (nonnegative : 0 ≤ ρ) (norm : (∑ i, |a i|) ≤ L)
    (near : ∀ i, |x i - y i| ≤ ρ) : |a ⬝ᵥ x - a ⬝ᵥ y| ≤ L * ρ

axiom central_buffer {n : ℕ} (a x z perturbed : Fin n → ℝ) (α Δ ρ L : ℝ)
    (nonnegative : 0 ≤ ρ) (norm : (∑ i, |a i|) ≤ L)
    (valid : a ⬝ᵥ z ≤ α) (gap : α + Δ ≤ a ⬝ᵥ x)
    (small : L * ρ ≤ Δ / 2) (near : ∀ i, |perturbed i - z i| ≤ ρ) :
    a ⬝ᵥ perturbed ≤ a ⬝ᵥ x - Δ / 2

axiom scaled_cleared_cut {n : ℕ} (positive : 0 < n) (a : Fin n → ℚ)
    (query z : Fin n → ℝ) (α Δ ρ L : ℝ)
    (nonnegative : 0 ≤ ρ) (norm : (∑ i, |(a i : ℝ)|) ≤ L)
    (valid : (fun i => (a i : ℝ)) ⬝ᵥ z ≤ α)
    (gap : α + Δ ≤ (fun i => (a i : ℝ)) ⬝ᵥ (fun i => 4 * (n : ℝ) * query i))
    (small : L * ρ ≤ Δ / 2) (e : Fin n → ℝ)
    (near : ∀ i, |e i| ≤ ρ / (4 * n)) :
    (fun i => (integerNormal a i : ℝ)) ⬝ᵥ
      (Lax263307.BufferedEllipsoid.scale z + e - query) ≤ 0

end Lax263307.RationalCutBuffer

  Real.instLE.le 0 ρ →
    Real.instLE.le (Finset.univ.sum fun i => abs (a i)) L →
      Real.instLE.le (dotProduct a z) α →

          Real.instLE.le (instHMul.hMul L ρ) (instHDiv.hDiv Δ 2) →

  instLTNat.lt 0 n →
    ∀ (a : Fin n → Rat) (query z : Fin n → Real) (α Δ ρ L : Real),
      Real.instLE.le 0 ρ →
        Real.instLE.le (Finset.univ.sum fun i => abs (a i).cast) L →
          Real.instLE.le (dotProduct (fun i => (a i).cast) z) α →
            Real.instLE.le (instHAdd.hAdd α Δ)

              Real.instLE.le (instHMul.hMul L ρ) (instHDiv.hDiv Δ 2) →

concepts.title: Rational LP certificates for distance projection
concepts.description:
Every valid exact certificate for the infinity-distance LP gives one of
three outcomes: the original relaxation is infeasible; a rational point
is feasible and within the prescribed coordinate error; or a rational
normal separates every feasible point with a gap exceeding that error.
The separating normal has sum of absolute coefficients at most one.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The objective of the projection LP is bounded, so an unbounded
certificate is impossible. Optimal primal and dual witnesses cast exactly
to real variables. This theorem checks the actual registered certificate
type; the dense matrix construction and solver RAM invocation still need
implementation.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.DistanceProjection
import Lax109476.CertificateSoundness

/-!
---
title: Rational LP certificates for distance projection
type: theorem
---
Every valid exact certificate for the infinity-distance LP gives one of
three outcomes: the original relaxation is infeasible; a rational point
is feasible and within the prescribed coordinate error; or a rational
normal separates every feasible point with a gap exceeding that error.
The separating normal has sum of absolute coefficients at most one.

# Formalization notes

The objective of the projection LP is bounded, so an unbounded
certificate is impossible. Optimal primal and dual witnesses cast exactly
to real variables. This theorem checks the actual registered certificate
type; the dense matrix construction and solver RAM invocation still need
implementation.
-/

namespace Lax263307.RationalProjection

open Lax109476.LinearProgram Lax109476.RationalCertificates
open Lax263307.DistanceProjection

inductive Outcome (n : ℕ)
  | near (point : Fin n → ℚ)
  | far (normal : Fin n → ℚ) (bound : ℚ)
  | reject

/-- Inspect the actual certificate and compare its distance by exact arithmetic. -/
def classify {m n : ℕ} (P : Program ℚ m n) (ρ : ℚ) :
    Certificate (m + (n + n)) (n + 1) → Outcome n
  | .optimal z dual =>
    if distance z ≤ ρ then .near (point z)
    else .far (normal dual) (dualValue P (oldMultipliers dual))
  | .infeasible _ => .reject
  | .unbounded _ _ => .reject

def Correct {m n : ℕ} (P : Program ℚ m n) (center : Fin n → ℚ) (ρ : ℚ) :
    Outcome n → Prop
  | .near y => PrimalFeasible (toReal P) (realVector y) ∧
      ∀ j, |(y j : ℝ) - (center j : ℝ)| ≤ (ρ : ℝ)
  | .far a α => (∑ j, |(a j : ℝ)|) ≤ 1 ∧
      (∀ y, PrimalFeasible (toReal P) y → (∑ j, (a j : ℝ) * y j) ≤ (α : ℝ)) ∧
      (ρ : ℝ) < (∑ j, (a j : ℝ) * (center j : ℝ)) - (α : ℝ)
  | .reject => ¬ IsFeasible (toReal P)

axiom classify_correct {m n : ℕ} (P : Program ℚ m n) (center : Fin n → ℚ) (ρ : ℚ)
    (certificate : Certificate (m + (n + n)) (n + 1))
    (valid : IsValidCertificate (distanceProgram P center) certificate) :
    Correct P center ρ (classify P ρ certificate)

axiom certificate_outcome {m n : ℕ} (P : Program ℚ m n) (center : Fin n → ℚ)
    (certificate : Certificate (m + (n + n)) (n + 1))
    (valid : IsValidCertificate (distanceProgram P center) certificate) (ρ : ℝ) :
    (¬ IsFeasible (toReal P)) ∨
      (∃ y : Fin n → ℚ, PrimalFeasible (toReal P) (realVector y) ∧
        ∀ j, |(y j : ℝ) - (center j : ℝ)| ≤ ρ) ∨
      (∃ a : Fin n → ℚ, ∃ α : ℚ,
        (∑ j, |(a j : ℝ)|) ≤ 1 ∧
        (∀ y, PrimalFeasible (toReal P) y → (∑ j, (a j : ℝ) * y j) ≤ (α : ℝ)) ∧
        ρ < (∑ j, (a j : ℝ) * (center j : ℝ)) - (α : ℝ))

end Lax263307.RationalProjection

certificate_outcome : ∀ {m n : Nat} (P : Lax109476.LinearProgram.Program Rat m n) (center : Fin n → Rat)
  (certificate : Lax109476.RationalCertificates.Certificate (instHAdd.hAdd m (instHAdd.hAdd n n)) (instHAdd.hAdd n 1)),
  Lax109476.RationalCertificates.IsValidCertificate (Lax263307.DistanceProjection.distanceProgram P center)
      certificate →
    ∀ (ρ : Real),
      Or (Not (Lax109476.LinearProgram.IsFeasible (Lax109476.RationalCertificates.toReal P)))
        (Or
          (Exists fun y =>
            And
              (Lax109476.LinearProgram.PrimalFeasible (Lax109476.RationalCertificates.toReal P)
                (Lax109476.RationalCertificates.realVector y))
              (∀ (j : Fin n), Real.instLE.le (abs (instHSub.hSub (y j).cast (center j).cast)) ρ))
          (Exists fun a =>
            Exists fun α =>
              And (Real.instLE.le (Finset.univ.sum fun j => abs (a j).cast) 1)
                (And
                  (∀ (y : Fin n → Real),
                    Lax109476.LinearProgram.PrimalFeasible (Lax109476.RationalCertificates.toReal P) y →
                      Real.instLE.le (Finset.univ.sum fun j => instHMul.hMul (a j).cast (y j)) α.cast)
                  (Real.instLT.lt ρ
                    (instHSub.hSub (Finset.univ.sum fun j => instHMul.hMul (a j).cast (center j).cast) α.cast)))))

classify_correct : ∀ {m n : Nat} (P : Lax109476.LinearProgram.Program Rat m n) (center : Fin n → Rat) (ρ : Rat)
  (certificate : Lax109476.RationalCertificates.Certificate (instHAdd.hAdd m (instHAdd.hAdd n n)) (instHAdd.hAdd n 1)),
  Lax109476.RationalCertificates.IsValidCertificate (Lax263307.DistanceProjection.distanceProgram P center)
      certificate →
    Lax263307.RationalProjection.Correct P center ρ (Lax263307.RationalProjection.classify P ρ certificate)

concepts.title: Depth and approximation loss of balanced recursion
concepts.description:
A recursive call on a balanced component has at most $\lfloor2n/3\rfloor$
vertices. The number of nontrivial calls on a branch is therefore logarithmic
in the original graph order. A factor $1-\delta$ lost at each of at most
$\lambda$ levels retains at least $1-\lambda\delta$ of a certified upper bound.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The integer depth function avoids numerical evaluation of logarithms with
base $3/2$. Empty graphs and singletons have depth zero. The explicit upper
bound uses twice the binary logarithm; this constant change does not affect
the QPTAS bound.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown:
Bonnet–Chang, the recursion-depth argument in Lemma 14 and Bernoulli's
inequality in Theorem 15.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.WeightedIndependentSet
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Log

/-!
---
title: Depth and approximation loss of balanced recursion
type: theorem
---
A recursive call on a balanced component has at most $\lfloor2n/3\rfloor$
vertices. The number of nontrivial calls on a branch is therefore logarithmic
in the original graph order. A factor $1-\delta$ lost at each of at most
$\lambda$ levels retains at least $1-\lambda\delta$ of a certified upper bound.

# Formalization notes

The integer depth function avoids numerical evaluation of logarithms with
base $3/2$. Empty graphs and singletons have depth zero. The explicit upper
bound uses twice the binary logarithm; this constant change does not affect
the QPTAS bound.

# Attribution

Bonnet–Chang, the recursion-depth argument in Lemma 14 and Bernoulli's
inequality in Theorem 15.
-/

namespace Lax263307.RecursionDepth

/-- Number of balanced reductions needed to reach order at most one. -/
def depth (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if n ≤ 1 then 0 else 1 + depth (2 * n / 3)
termination_by n
decreasing_by omega

/-- A balanced recursive call consumes one level. -/
axiom balanced_decrease (n m : ℕ) (nontrivial : 1 < n) (balanced : 3 * m ≤ 2 * n) :
    depth m + 1 ≤ depth n

/-- At most two reductions are needed per binary-logarithm level. -/
axiom logarithmic_bound (n : ℕ) : depth n ≤ 2 * (Nat.log2 n + 1)

/-- A certified independence upper bound turns the accumulated loss into approximation. -/
axiom approximation_transfer {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (I : Finset (Fin n)) (u levels : ℕ) (δ ε : ℚ)
    (independent : G.IsIndepSet (I : Set (Fin n)))
    (upper_bound : ∀ J : Finset (Fin n), G.IsIndepSet (J : Set (Fin n)) → J.card ≤ u)
    (δ_nonnegative : 0 ≤ δ) (δ_small : δ ≤ 1)
    (ε_small : ε ≤ 1) (loss : (levels : ℚ) * δ ≤ ε)
    (size : (1 - δ) ^ levels * (u : ℚ) ≤ I.card) :
    WeightedIndependentSet.IsApproximation G (fun _ => 1) ε I

end Lax263307.RecursionDepth

  G.IsIndepSet (Finset.instSetLike.coe I) →
    (∀ (J : Finset (Fin n)), G.IsIndepSet (Finset.instSetLike.coe J) → instLENat.le J.card u) →
      Rat.instLE.le 0 δ →
        Rat.instLE.le δ 1 →
          Rat.instLE.le ε 1 →
            Rat.instLE.le (instHMul.hMul levels.cast δ) ε →
              Rat.instLE.le (instHMul.hMul (instHPow.hPow (instHSub.hSub 1 δ) levels) u.cast) I.card.cast →
                Lax263307.WeightedIndependentSet.IsApproximation G (fun x => 1) ε I

concepts.title: Correctness of the complete recursive unweighted algorithm
concepts.description:
An explicit recursive function uses exhaustive search for small targets and
bounded projected round-or-cut search for larger targets. Child calls operate
on canonically labeled balanced parts. Descending target search returns an
independent set with the requested approximation ratio.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The depth budget terminates every call. Induction discharges the child-query
hypothesis of the projected oracle, including sound rejection. The accuracy
denominator is 4(depth(n)+1)ceil(1/epsilon). This proves correctness of the
computable function; a finite RAM implementation and its uniform complexity
bound are still needed for the main theorem.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.ProjectedOracle
import Lax263307.ExhaustiveTargets
import Lax263307.RecursionDepth
import Lax263307.TargetSearch

/-!
---
title: Correctness of the complete recursive unweighted algorithm
type: theorem
---
An explicit recursive function uses exhaustive search for small targets and
bounded projected round-or-cut search for larger targets. Child calls operate
on canonically labeled balanced parts. Descending target search returns an
independent set with the requested approximation ratio.

# Formalization notes

The depth budget terminates every call. Induction discharges the child-query
hypothesis of the projected oracle, including sound rejection. The accuracy
denominator is 4(depth(n)+1)ceil(1/epsilon). This proves correctness of the
computable function; a finite RAM implementation and its uniform complexity
bound are still needed for the main theorem.
-/

namespace Lax263307.RecursiveAlgorithm

open ComputedSeparators AlgorithmParameters

def attempt (lp flow : List ℕ → List ℕ) (a K B D : ℕ) (fuel : ℕ)
    {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (k : ℕ) : Option (Finset (Fin n)) :=
  if k ≤ cutoff a K B n D ∨ n ≤ 1 then ExhaustiveTargets.findIndependentSet G k
  else if n < k then none
  else match fuel with
    | 0 => none
    | fuel + 1 => ProjectedOracle.search lp flow a K B D G k
        (fun C t => (attempt lp flow a K B D fuel (restriction G C) t).map
          (fun I => I.image (label C)))
termination_by fuel

def solve {n : ℕ} (lp flow : List ℕ → List ℕ) (a K B D : ℕ)
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : Finset (Fin n) × ℕ :=
  TargetSearch.search (attempt lp flow a K B D (RecursionDepth.depth n) G) n

def Correct {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (k fuel D : ℕ) : Option (Finset (Fin n)) → Prop
  | some I => G.IsIndepSet (I : Set (Fin n)) ∧ (1 - 4*(1/(D:ℝ)))^fuel * (k:ℝ) ≤ I.card
  | none => ∀ J : Finset (Fin n), G.IsIndepSet (J : Set (Fin n)) → J.card < k

def accuracyDenominator (n : ℕ) (ε : ℚ) : ℕ :=
  4 * (RecursionDepth.depth n + 1) * ⌈ε⁻¹⌉₊

def independentSet {n : ℕ} (lp flow : List ℕ → List ℕ) (a K B : ℕ)
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (ε : ℚ) : Finset (Fin n) :=
  (solve lp flow a K B (accuracyDenominator n ε) G).1

open GraphClasses PowerBagBounds

axiom exists_solver (C : GraphClass) (hereditary : IsHereditary C)
    (a A : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) (hA : 0 < A) (class_bound : HasPowerBagBound C a A) :
    ∃ (lp flow : List ℕ → List ℕ) (K B : ℕ),
      Lax759944.RamPolytime.RamPolytime lp ∧ Lax759944.RamPolytime.RamPolytime flow ∧
      0 < K ∧ 0 < B ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      G ∈ C n → ∀ ε : ℚ, 0 < ε → ε < 1 →
      Lax263307.WeightedIndependentSet.IsApproximation G (fun _ => 1) ε
        (independentSet lp flow a K B G ε)

end Lax263307.RecursiveAlgorithm

statements.signature:
exists_solver : ∀ (C : Lax263307.GraphClasses.GraphClass),
  Lax263307.GraphClasses.IsHereditary C →
    ∀ (a A : Nat),
      instLTNat.lt 0 a →
        instLTNat.lt 0 A →
          Lax263307.PowerBagBounds.HasPowerBagBound C a A →
            Exists fun lp =>
              Exists fun flow =>
                Exists fun K =>
                  Exists fun B =>
                    And (Lax759944.RamPolytime.RamPolytime lp)
                      (And (Lax759944.RamPolytime.RamPolytime flow)
                        (And (instLTNat.lt 0 K)
                          (And (instLTNat.lt 0 B)
                            (∀ (n : Nat) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [inst : DecidableRel G.Adj],
                              Set.instMembership.mem (C n) G →
                                ∀ (ε : Rat),
                                  Rat.instLT.lt 0 ε →
                                    Rat.instLT.lt ε 1 →
                                      Lax263307.WeightedIndependentSet.IsApproximation G (fun x => 1) ε
                                        (Lax263307.RecursiveAlgorithm.independentSet lp flow a K B G ε)))))

concepts.title: Combining recursive answers in round-or-cut
concepts.description:
Suppose conditioning gives costs of total mass $k$, and the deleted
separator has cost at most $\delta k$. Each remaining part returns an
independent set of size at least $(1-\delta)^h u_C$, where $u_C$ bounds
the part's independence number. Either some conditioned part cost exceeds
$u_C$, giving a valid violated cut, or the union of the returned sets is

import Lax263307.SeparatorComponents
import Lax263307.ComponentCuts

/-!
---
title: Combining recursive answers in round-or-cut
type: theorem
---
Suppose conditioning gives costs of total mass $k$, and the deleted
separator has cost at most $\delta k$. Each remaining part returns an
independent set of size at least $(1-\delta)^h u_C$, where $u_C$ bounds
the part's independence number. Either some conditioned part cost exceeds
$u_C$, giving a valid violated cut, or the union of the returned sets is
independent and has size at least $(1-\delta)^{h+1}k$.

# Attribution

Bonnet–Chang, equation (24) and the round-or-cut step in Lemma 14.
-/

namespace Lax263307.RecursiveRounding

open LinearRelaxation SeparatorComponents

/-- Independent answers on different parts combine, and their sizes add. -/
axiom combine_independent {n : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (P : Partition G S ι)
    (I : ι → Finset (Fin n)) (inside : ∀ i, I i ⊆ P.vertices i)
    (independent : ∀ i, G.IsIndepSet (I i : Set (Fin n))) :
    G.IsIndepSet (combine I : Set (Fin n)) ∧ (combine I).card = ∑ i, (I i).card

/-- One query returns a sufficiently large set or a valid separating inequality. -/
axiom round_or_cut {n r : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (k h : ℕ) (δ : ℝ)
    (δ_nonnegative : 0 ≤ δ) (δ_small : δ ≤ 1)
    (y : MomentVector n r) (A S : Finset (Fin n)) (P : Partition G S ι)
    (size : A.card ≤ r) (positive : 0 < value y A)
    (mass : (∑ v, conditioned y A v) = k)
    (light : ∑ v ∈ S, conditioned y A v ≤ δ * k)
    (I : ι → Finset (Fin n)) (u : ι → ℕ)
    (inside : ∀ i, I i ⊆ P.vertices i)
    (independent : ∀ i, G.IsIndepSet (I i : Set (Fin n)))
    (bounds : ∀ i, IsIndependenceBound G (P.vertices i) (u i))
    (approximation : ∀ i, (1 - δ) ^ h * (u i : ℝ) ≤ (I i).card) :
    (G.IsIndepSet (combine I : Set (Fin n)) ∧
      (1 - δ) ^ (h + 1) * (k : ℝ) ≤ (combine I).card) ∨
    ∃ i, (∀ z ∈ independentSetHull G k r,
      ∑ v ∈ P.vertices i, value z (insert v A) ≤ (u i : ℝ) * value z A) ∧
      (u i : ℝ) * value y A < ∑ v ∈ P.vertices i, value y (insert v A)

end Lax263307.RecursiveRounding

concepts.title: Decoding the actual registered LP solver output
concepts.description:
Read the tagged rational certificate returned by the registered exact LP
solver. The decoded certificate is valid for the supplied program, in all
dimensions and for all three outcomes. This provides the concrete solver
function used by the projection branch of the round-or-cut algorithm.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The parser and fallback are total and computable. The fallback is never used
on the registered solver's output. The parser matches the verified parser
in the registered Leighton–Rao proof package; an induction identifies the
parsers and reuses its encoding theorem. The surrounding RAM invocation remains a separate
implementation obligation.

namespace Lax263307.RegisteredLP

open Lax109476.LinearProgram Lax109476.RationalCertificates Lax109476.RationalEncoding

def value (sign num den : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  if sign = 1 then -(num : ℚ) / den else (num : ℚ) / den

def rational : List ℕ → Option (ℚ × List ℕ)
  | sign :: num :: den :: rest => some (value sign num den, rest)
  | _ => none

def vector : ℕ → List ℕ → Option (List ℚ × List ℕ)
  | 0, input => some ([], input)
  | n + 1, input => (rational input).bind fun qr =>
      (vector n qr.2).map fun tail => (qr.1 :: tail.1, tail.2)

def vectorFunction (n : ℕ) (input : List ℕ) : Option ((Fin n → ℚ) × List ℕ) :=
  (vector n input).map fun result => (fun i => result.1.getD i.val 0, result.2)

def parse (m n : ℕ) : List ℕ → Option (Certificate m n × List ℕ)
  | 0 :: rest => (vectorFunction n rest).bind fun zr =>
      (vectorFunction m zr.2).map fun yr => (.optimal zr.1 yr.1, yr.2)
  | 1 :: rest => (vectorFunction m rest).map fun yr => (.infeasible yr.1, yr.2)
  | 2 :: rest => (vectorFunction n rest).bind fun zr =>
      (vectorFunction n zr.2).map fun dr => (.unbounded zr.1 dr.1, dr.2)
  | _ => none

def certificate {m n : ℕ} (solve : List ℕ → List ℕ) (P : Program ℚ m n) : Certificate m n :=
  ((parse m n (solve (encodeProgram P))).map Prod.fst).getD (.infeasible 0)

axiom exists_solver : ∃ solve : List ℕ → List ℕ, Lax759944.RamPolytime.RamPolytime solve ∧
    ∀ (m n : ℕ) (P : Program ℚ m n), IsValidCertificate P (certificate solve P)

end Lax263307.RegisteredLP

concepts.description:
Suppose repeated cuts of an $n$-vertex graph discard pairwise disjoint
shores $B_i$, and each separator $A_i\cap B_i$ has cost at most
$4\rho|A_i||B_i|/\gamma$. Nonnegative costs imply that the union of all
these separators has total cost at most $4\rho n^2/\gamma$.

type: theorem

Suppose repeated cuts of an $n$-vertex graph discard pairwise disjoint
shores $B_i$, and each separator $A_i\cap B_i$ has cost at most
$4\rho|A_i||B_i|/\gamma$. Nonnegative costs imply that the union of all
these separators has total cost at most $4\rho n^2/\gamma$.

namespace Lax263307.RepeatedCutAccounting

noncomputable def cost {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : ℝ := ∑ v ∈ S, x v

axiom total_cut_cost {n q : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℝ) (nonnegative : ∀ v, 0 ≤ x v)
    (A B : Fin q → Finset (Fin n)) (disjoint : Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint (B i) (B j))
    (ρ γ : ℝ) (rho_nonnegative : 0 ≤ ρ) (gamma_positive : 0 < γ)
    (each_cut : ∀ i, cost x (A i ∩ B i) ≤ 4 * ρ * (A i).card * (B i).card / γ) :
    cost x (Finset.univ.biUnion fun i => A i ∩ B i) ≤ 4 * ρ * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / γ

end Lax263307.RepeatedCutAccounting

import Lax263307.BufferedEllipsoid
import Lax109476.RationalEncoding
import Mathlib.Data.Rat.Floor
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Sqrt
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Size

/-!
---
title: A bounded rounded ellipsoid search with answer-or-cut replies
type: theorem
---
An oracle returns an answer, a certified rejection, or a nonzero integer
central-cut normal. The search stores a rational matrix and center, advances
them once per cut, and stops after an explicit finite iteration budget.
When rejection is impossible and every cut preserves a fixed dyadic cube
around a scaled unit-cube point, the search must return an answer.

# Formalization notes

The computable rational update is the registered LP ellipsoid update,
written explicitly so that definitions and statement types do not import
a proof package. The proof identifies its trajectory with the registered
sequence and applies that sequence's determinant and containment theorems.
This is a functional search; its oracle and RAM refinements are separate
implementation obligations.
-/

namespace Lax263307.RoundedOracleSearch

open Matrix

abbrev State (n : ℕ) := Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℚ × (Fin n → ℚ)

inductive Reply (n : ℕ) (Result : Type)
  | found (answer : Result)
  | reject
  | cut (normal : Fin n → ℤ)

def rationalNormal {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n → ℤ) : Fin n → ℚ := fun i => a i

def roundDown (q : ℚ) (D : ℕ) : ℚ := (Int.floor (q * D) : ℚ) / D

def sqrtUpper (q : ℚ) (D : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  ((Nat.sqrt (Nat.ceil (q * (D : ℚ) ^ 2)) + 1 : ℕ) : ℚ) / D

def cutShape {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℚ) (a : Fin n → ℚ) :
    Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℚ :=
  ((n : ℚ) ^ 2 / ((n : ℚ) ^ 2 - 1)) •
    (A - (2 / (((n : ℚ) + 1) * (a ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ a)))) •
      Matrix.vecMulVec (A *ᵥ a) (A *ᵥ a))

def grid (n k : ℕ) : ℕ := 2 ^ ((2 * k + 2) + (2 * n + 4) + n + 3)

def cached {n : ℕ} (state : State n) : State n :=
  let rows : Vector (Vector ℚ n) n := Vector.ofFn (fun i => Vector.ofFn (state.1 i))
  let center : Vector ℚ n := Vector.ofFn state.2
  ((fun i j => (rows.get i).get j), fun i => center.get i)

def update {n : ℕ} (k : ℕ) (state : State n) (a : Fin n → ℤ) : State n :=
  let a := rationalNormal a
  let D := grid n k
  let η : ℚ := 1 / (2 : ℚ) ^ (2 * n + 4)
  let shape := ((1 + η) ^ 2) •
    ((Matrix.of fun i j => roundDown (cutShape state.1 a i j) D) + ((n : ℚ) / D) • 1)
  let center := fun i => roundDown
    (state.2 i - (1 / (((n : ℚ) + 1) * sqrtUpper (a ⬝ᵥ (state.1 *ᵥ a)) D)) *
      (state.1 *ᵥ a) i) D
  cached (shape, center)

def fallback {n : ℕ} : Fin n → ℤ := fun i => if i.val = 0 then 1 else 0

def selectedNormal {n : ℕ} {Result : Type} : Reply n Result → Fin n → ℤ
  | .cut a => a
  | _ => fallback

def trajectory {n : ℕ} {Result : Type} (oracle : ℕ → (Fin n → ℚ) → Reply n Result) :
    ℕ → State n
  | 0 => (1, 0)
  | k + 1 =>
    let old := trajectory oracle k
    update k old (selectedNormal (oracle k old.2))

def normalSchedule {n : ℕ} {Result : Type}
    (oracle : ℕ → (Fin n → ℚ) → Reply n Result) (k : ℕ) : Fin n → ℤ :=
  selectedNormal (oracle k (trajectory oracle k).2)

def scan {n : ℕ} {Result : Type} (oracle : ℕ → (Fin n → ℚ) → Reply n Result) :
    ℕ → ℕ → State n → Option Result
  | _, 0, _ => none
  | k, count + 1, state =>
    match oracle k state.2 with
    | .found answer => some answer
    | .reject => none
    | .cut a => scan oracle (k + 1) count (update k state a)

def steps (n B : ℕ) : ℕ := 4 * (n + 1) * (B * n + 1)

def search {n : ℕ} {Result : Type} (oracle : ℕ → (Fin n → ℚ) → Reply n Result)
    (B : ℕ) : Option Result := scan oracle 0 (steps n B) (1, 0)

axiom search_sound {n : ℕ} {Result : Type}
    (oracle : ℕ → (Fin n → ℚ) → Reply n Result) (B : ℕ) (Good : Result → Prop)
    (answers : ∀ k center answer, oracle k center = .found answer → Good answer) :
    ∀ answer, search oracle B = some answer → Good answer

axiom search_complete {n : ℕ} {Result : Type} (dimension : 2 ≤ n)
    (oracle : ℕ → (Fin n → ℚ) → Reply n Result) (B : ℕ) (precision : 2 ≤ B)
    (nonzero : ∀ k center a, oracle k center = .cut a → ∃ i, a i ≠ 0)
    (no_reject : ∀ k center, oracle k center ≠ .reject)
    (z : Fin n → ℝ) (cube : ∀ i, 0 ≤ z i ∧ z i ≤ 1)
    (retains : ∀ k center a, oracle k center = .cut a →
      ∀ e : Fin n → ℝ, (∀ i, |e i| ≤ ((2 : ℝ) ^ B)⁻¹) →
        (fun i => (a i : ℝ)) ⬝ᵥ
          (Lax263307.BufferedEllipsoid.scale z + e - (fun i => (center i : ℝ))) ≤ 0) :
    ∃ answer, search oracle B = some answer

axiom center_encoding_bound {n : ℕ} {Result : Type} (dimension : 2 ≤ n)
    (oracle : ℕ → (Fin n → ℚ) → Reply n Result)
    (nonzero : ∀ k center a, oracle k center = .cut a → ∃ i, a i ≠ 0) (k : ℕ) (i : Fin n) :
    Lax759944.BinaryWordEncoding.bitSize
      (Lax109476.RationalEncoding.encodeRational ((trajectory oracle k).2 i)) ≤ 60 + 6 * k + 14 * n

axiom shape_encoding_bound {n : ℕ} {Result : Type} (dimension : 2 ≤ n)
    (oracle : ℕ → (Fin n → ℚ) → Reply n Result)
    (nonzero : ∀ k center a, oracle k center = .cut a → ∃ i, a i ≠ 0)
    (k : ℕ) (i j : Fin n) :
    Lax759944.BinaryWordEncoding.bitSize
      (Lax109476.RationalEncoding.encodeRational ((trajectory oracle k).1 i j)) ≤ 60 + 6 * k + 14 * n

end Lax263307.RoundedOracleSearch

            ∀ (z : Fin n → Real),

                          Real.instLE.le
                            (dotProduct (fun i => (a i).cast)
                              (instHSub.hSub (instHAdd.hAdd (Lax263307.BufferedEllipsoid.scale z) e) fun i =>

  (Good : Result → Prop),
  (∀ (k : Nat) (center : Fin n → Rat) (answer : Result),
      Eq (oracle k center) (Lax263307.RoundedOracleSearch.Reply.found answer) → Good answer) →
    ∀ (answer : Result), Eq (Lax263307.RoundedOracleSearch.search oracle B) (Option.some answer) → Good answer

    ∀ (oracle : Nat → (Fin n → Rat) → Lax263307.RoundedOracleSearch.Reply n Result),
      (∀ (k : Nat) (center : Fin n → Rat) (a : Fin n → Int),
          Eq (oracle k center) (Lax263307.RoundedOracleSearch.Reply.cut a) → Exists fun i => Ne (a i) 0) →

concepts.title: Rounding loses at most one weight unit per vertex
concepts.description:
For nonnegative weights and $\tau>0$, the multiplicities
$t_v=\lfloor w_v/\tau\rfloor$ satisfy
$$w_v-\tau\le\tau t_v\le w_v.$$
Consequently, for each vertex set $J$,
$$\tau\sum_{v\in J}t_v\ge w(J)-|J|\tau.$$
With $\tau=\varepsilon W/(2n)$, the total number of copies is at most
$2n^2/\varepsilon$.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown: Bonnet–Chang, proof of Theorem 2 in Section 6.

/-!

title: Rounding loses at most one weight unit per vertex
type: theorem
---
For nonnegative weights and $\tau>0$, the multiplicities
$t_v=\lfloor w_v/\tau\rfloor$ satisfy
$$w_v-\tau\le\tau t_v\le w_v.$$
Consequently, for each vertex set $J$,
$$\tau\sum_{v\in J}t_v\ge w(J)-|J|\tau.$$

namespace Lax263307.RoundingBounds

open WeightedIndependentSet WeightRounding

/-- The floor approximation loses at most one positive scaling unit. -/
axiom pointwise_bounds {n : ℕ} (w : Fin n → ℚ) (τ : ℚ)
    (nonnegative : ∀ v, 0 ≤ w v) (positive_scale : 0 < τ) :
    ∀ v, τ * (roundedCopies w τ v : ℚ) ≤ w v ∧
      w v - τ ≤ τ * (roundedCopies w τ v : ℚ)

/-- The additive rounding loss is at most the set cardinality times the scaling unit. -/
axiom set_rounding_loss {n : ℕ} (w : Fin n → ℚ) (τ : ℚ)
    (nonnegative : ∀ v, 0 ≤ w v) (positive_scale : 0 < τ) (J : Finset (Fin n)) :
    weight w J - (J.card : ℚ) * τ ≤ τ * ((∑ v ∈ J, roundedCopies w τ v : ℕ) : ℚ)

/-- The rounded blow-up order is polynomial in the order and inverse accuracy. -/
axiom total_copy_bound {n : ℕ} (w : Fin n → ℚ) (ε : ℚ)
    (nonnegative : ∀ v, 0 ≤ w v) (positive_order : 0 < n)
    (positive_accuracy : 0 < ε) (positive_maximum : 0 < maximumWeight w) :
    ((∑ v, copies w ε v : ℕ) : ℚ) ≤ 2 * (n : ℚ) ^ 2 / ε

end Lax263307.RoundingBounds

concepts.title: Graph-route distributions from high-value split flows
concepts.description:
A feasible directed split flow of value at least $1/\gamma$ yields a finite
distribution of simple original graph routes with uniform ordered endpoints.
The probability that a route uses vertex $v$ is at most
$\gamma x_v/n^2$. Both endpoints count toward this load; equal original
endpoints are allowed and their route is a singleton.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Routes carrying positive probability are simple graph paths. Zero-probability
outcomes may have empty routes. Arc-to-path conversion is used only for the
existence argument, so this statement imposes no algorithm for constructing
the distribution. The underlying solver still returns an arc-flow certificate.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown: Bonnet–Chang, flow normalization and endpoint-inclusive loads in Lemma 7.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.RoutingNormalization
import Lax263307.SplitPathProjection

/-!
---
title: Graph-route distributions from high-value split flows
type: theorem
---
A feasible directed split flow of value at least $1/\gamma$ yields a finite
distribution of simple original graph routes with uniform ordered endpoints.
The probability that a route uses vertex $v$ is at most
$\gamma x_v/n^2$. Both endpoints count toward this load; equal original
endpoints are allowed and their route is a singleton.

# Formalization notes

Routes carrying positive probability are simple graph paths. Zero-probability
outcomes may have empty routes. Arc-to-path conversion is used only for the
existence argument, so this statement imposes no algorithm for constructing
the distribution. The underlying solver still returns an arc-flow certificate.

# Attribution

Bonnet–Chang, flow normalization and endpoint-inclusive loads in Lemma 7.
-/

namespace Lax263307.RouteDistributions

open scoped NNReal NNRat
open Lax263307.RoutingNormalization Lax263307.VertexSplitting
open Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow

structure Distribution {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (q : ℕ) where
  probability : Fin q → ℝ
  nonnegative : ∀ i, 0 ≤ probability i
  normalized : (∑ i, probability i) = 1
  route : Fin q → List (Fin n)
  valid : ∀ i, 0 < probability i → (route i).Nodup ∧ (route i).IsChain G.Adj ∧ route i ≠ []
  uniform : ∀ u v, (∑ i, if (route i).head? = some u ∧ (route i).getLast? = some v then
    probability i else 0) = 1 / (n : ℝ) ^ 2

noncomputable def Distribution.toSampling {n q : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)}
    (D : Distribution G q) : Lax263307.PathSampling.Distribution n q where
  probability := D.probability
  nonnegative := D.nonnegative
  normalized := D.normalized
  vertices i := (D.route i).toFinset

/-- Normalize finite graph routes commodity by commodity. -/
axiom finite_routes {n q : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (hn : 0 < n)
    (w : Fin q → ℝ) (E : Fin n → Fin n → Fin q → Prop)
    (w_nonnegative : ∀ i, 0 ≤ w i) (γ : ℝ) (γ_positive : 0 < γ)
    (lower : ∀ u v, 1 / γ ≤ routed w E u v)
    (Q : Fin q → List (Fin n))
    (routes : ∀ u v i, E u v i → (Q i).Nodup ∧ (Q i).IsChain G.Adj ∧
      (Q i).head? = some u ∧ (Q i).getLast? = some v) :
    ∃ D : Distribution G (n * (n * q)), ∀ z,
      Lax263307.PathSampling.load D.toSampling z ≤ γ / (n : ℝ) ^ 2 *
        (∑ i, w i * (if z ∈ Q i then (1 : ℝ) else 0))

/-- A high-value split arc-flow certificate yields a bounded-load route distribution. -/
axiom split_arc_distribution {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℚ≥0) (large : ℚ≥0) (γ : ℝ) (γ_positive : 0 < γ)
    (f : ℝ≥0) (high : 1 / γ ≤ (f : ℝ)) (F : ArcFlow (2 * n))
    (feasible : IsArcConcurrentFlow .directed (splitInstance G x large).network
      (splitInstance G x large).weights f F) :
    ∃ q, ∃ D : Distribution G q, ∀ z,
      Lax263307.PathSampling.load D.toSampling z ≤ γ * (x z : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) ^ 2

end Lax263307.RouteDistributions

concepts.title: Discarding long almost-embedding routes
concepts.description:
Discard each source edge whose host route uses more than $L$ vertices. The
number of discarded edges times $L$ is at most the original total route
size. The remaining graph retains an induced almost-embedding with every
route using at most $L$ vertices. Edge deletion may create isolated source
vertices; the transfer with singleton bags handles them separately.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown: Bonnet–Chang, the long-route deletion step in Lemma 11.

import Lax263307.AlmostEmbeddings
import Lax263307.EdgeDeletionWidth

/-!
---
title: Discarding long almost-embedding routes
type: theorem
---
Discard each source edge whose host route uses more than $L$ vertices. The
number of discarded edges times $L$ is at most the original total route
size. The remaining graph retains an induced almost-embedding with every
route using at most $L$ vertices. Edge deletion may create isolated source
vertices; the transfer with singleton bags handles them separately.

# Attribution

Bonnet–Chang, the long-route deletion step in Lemma 11.

namespace Lax263307.RoutePruning

open Lax263307.AlmostEmbeddings

noncomputable def longEdges {t n : ℕ} {H : SimpleGraph (Fin t)} [DecidableRel H.Adj]
    {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)} (E : AlmostEmbedding H G) (L : ℕ) : Finset (Sym2 (Fin t)) := by
  classical
  exact (Finset.univ.filter fun e : H.edgeSet => L < (E.route e).card).image Subtype.val

axiom long_edge_count {t n : ℕ} (H : SimpleGraph (Fin t)) [DecidableRel H.Adj]
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (E : AlmostEmbedding H G) (L : ℕ) :
    L * (longEdges E L).card ≤ ∑ e : H.edgeSet, (E.route e).card

axiom prune_routes {t n : ℕ} (H : SimpleGraph (Fin t)) [DecidableRel H.Adj]
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (E : AlmostEmbedding H G) (induced : IsInduced E) (L : ℕ) :
    ∃ E' : AlmostEmbedding (H.deleteEdges (↑(longEdges E L) : Set (Sym2 (Fin t)))) G,
      IsInduced E' ∧ (∀ e, (E'.route e).card ≤ L)

end Lax263307.RoutePruning

concepts.title: Uniform endpoint normalization of finite path flows
concepts.description:
Normalize each of the $n^2$ ordered endpoint commodities to mass $1/n^2$.
If every commodity has routed mass at least $1/\gamma$, normalization
increases any nonnegative load by at most $\gamma/n^2$. Each flow record
belongs to at most one endpoint pair, so records are counted only once.
The statement includes diagonal commodities and applies to vertex loads
that count both route endpoints.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown: Bonnet–Chang, normalization and vertex-load accounting in Lemma 7.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.PathSampling

/-!
---
title: Uniform endpoint normalization of finite path flows
type: theorem
---
Normalize each of the $n^2$ ordered endpoint commodities to mass $1/n^2$.
If every commodity has routed mass at least $1/\gamma$, normalization
increases any nonnegative load by at most $\gamma/n^2$. Each flow record
belongs to at most one endpoint pair, so records are counted only once.
The statement includes diagonal commodities and applies to vertex loads
that count both route endpoints.

# Attribution

Bonnet–Chang, normalization and vertex-load accounting in Lemma 7.
-/

namespace Lax263307.RoutingNormalization

def IsUniquePair {n q : ℕ} (E : Fin n → Fin n → Fin q → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ i u v u' v', E u v i → E u' v' i → u = u' ∧ v = v'

noncomputable def routed {n q : ℕ} (w : Fin q → ℝ)
    (E : Fin n → Fin n → Fin q → Prop) (u v : Fin n) : ℝ := by
  classical
  exact ∑ i, if E u v i then w i else 0

noncomputable def probability {n q : ℕ} (w : Fin q → ℝ)
    (E : Fin n → Fin n → Fin q → Prop) (u v : Fin n) (i : Fin q) : ℝ := by
  classical
  exact if E u v i then w i / (routed w E u v * (n : ℝ) ^ 2) else 0

/-- Nonnegative normalized probabilities with uniform ordered endpoints. -/
axiom normalization_correct {n q : ℕ} (w : Fin q → ℝ)
    (E : Fin n → Fin n → Fin q → Prop) (hn : 0 < n)
    (nonnegative : ∀ i, 0 ≤ w i) (positive : ∀ u v, 0 < routed w E u v) :
    (∀ u v i, 0 ≤ probability w E u v i) ∧
      (∀ u v, (∑ i, probability w E u v i) = 1 / (n : ℝ) ^ 2) ∧
      (∑ u, ∑ v, ∑ i, probability w E u v i) = 1

/-- Uniform commodity normalization preserves the scaled load bound. -/
axiom normalized_load_bound {n q : ℕ} (w : Fin q → ℝ)
    (E : Fin n → Fin n → Fin q → Prop) (hn : 0 < n)
    (nonnegative : ∀ i, 0 ≤ w i) (unique : IsUniquePair E)
    (γ : ℝ) (γ_positive : 0 < γ) (lower_bound : ∀ u v, 1 / γ ≤ routed w E u v)
    (cost : Fin q → ℝ) (cost_nonnegative : ∀ i, 0 ≤ cost i) :
    (∑ u, ∑ v, ∑ i, probability w E u v i * cost i) ≤
      γ / (n : ℝ) ^ 2 * (∑ i, w i * cost i)

end Lax263307.RoutingNormalization

concepts.title: An induced almost-embedding from a good route sample
concepts.description:
Sample the edges of any finite simple source graph from a uniform-endpoint
route distribution. If the interaction union bound is at most $1/4$ and
the expected total route size is at most $M>0$, some sample gives an induced
almost-embedding of total route size at most $4M$.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Enumerate unordered source edges only for the finite sampling construction.
Their two endpoints are distinct, and nonincident edges have four distinct
endpoints. A sampled route's ordered vertex list is a graph walk, so its
vertex set induces a connected graph. The shared vertex-image assignment
provides the endpoint condition in the almost-embedding.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown: Bonnet–Chang, the initial induced almost-embedding in Lemma 11.

title: An induced almost-embedding from a good route sample
type: theorem

the expected total route size is at most $M>0$, some sample gives an induced

# Formalization notes

Enumerate unordered source edges only for the finite sampling construction.
Their two endpoints are distinct, and nonincident edges have four distinct
endpoints. A sampled route's ordered vertex list is a graph walk, so its
vertex set induces a connected graph. The shared vertex-image assignment
provides the endpoint condition in the almost-embedding.

# Attribution

concepts.title: Choosing a collision-free outcome with bounded total path length
concepts.description:
For a finite probability distribution, suppose the probability of a bad
outcome is at most $1/4$ and a nonnegative total cost has expectation at most
$M>0$. Some outcome of positive probability is not bad and has total cost
at most $4M$. This combines the union bound with Markov's inequality.

sections.markdown:
Bonnet–Chang, the simultaneous choice of noninteracting routes and bounded
total path length in Lemma 11.

import Lax263307.PathSampling

/-!
---
title: Choosing a collision-free outcome with bounded total path length
type: theorem
---
For a finite probability distribution, suppose the probability of a bad
outcome is at most $1/4$ and a nonnegative total cost has expectation at most
$M>0$. Some outcome of positive probability is not bad and has total cost
at most $4M$. This combines the union bound with Markov's inequality.

# Attribution

Bonnet–Chang, the simultaneous choice of noninteracting routes and bounded
total path length in Lemma 11.
-/

namespace Lax263307.SamplingOutcomes

open PathSampling

/-- Probability of an event in the finite outcome space. -/
noncomputable def eventProbability {n q : ℕ} (P : Distribution n q)
    (event : Set (Fin q)) : ℝ := by
  classical
  exact ∑ i, if i ∈ event then P.probability i else 0

/-- Markov's inequality for a nonnegative cost and a positive threshold. -/
axiom markov_bound {n q : ℕ} (P : Distribution n q) (cost : Fin q → ℝ)
    (nonnegative : ∀ i, 0 ≤ cost i) (T : ℝ) (positive : 0 < T) :
    eventProbability P {i | T < cost i} ≤ (∑ i, P.probability i * cost i) / T

/-- One positive-probability outcome meets both requirements. -/
axiom good_outcome {n q : ℕ} (P : Distribution n q) (bad : Set (Fin q))
    (cost : Fin q → ℝ) (M : ℝ) (positive : 0 < M)
    (nonnegative : ∀ i, 0 ≤ cost i)
    (bad_bound : eventProbability P bad ≤ 1 / 4)
    (expected_bound : (∑ i, P.probability i * cost i) ≤ M) :
    ∃ i, 0 < P.probability i ∧ i ∉ bad ∧ cost i ≤ 4 * M

end Lax263307.SamplingOutcomes

concepts.title: The components left by deleting a separator
concepts.description:
Deleting a vertex set $S$ partitions the remaining vertices into connected
components. Every undeleted vertex belongs to exactly one part, and every
edge with undeleted endpoints has both endpoints in one part. These are the
properties used to combine the recursive independent sets.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
`Partition` also permits grouping connected components together. The canonical
`components` construction uses precisely the connected components of $G-S$.
The vertex sets of the parts are finite sets in the original vertex type.

Deleting a vertex set $S$ partitions the remaining vertices into connected
components. Every undeleted vertex belongs to exactly one part, and every
edge with undeleted endpoints has both endpoints in one part. These are the
properties used to combine the recursive independent sets.

# Formalization notes

`Partition` also permits grouping connected components together. The canonical
`components` construction uses precisely the connected components of $G-S$.
The vertex sets of the parts are finite sets in the original vertex type.
-/

namespace Lax263307.SeparatorComponents

/-- A partition of the undeleted vertices, closed under undeleted edges. -/
structure Partition {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (S : Finset (Fin n)) (ι : Type) where
  /-- The original vertices in each part. -/
  vertices : ι → Finset (Fin n)
  /-- Parts exclude the deleted vertices. -/
  outside : ∀ i v, v ∈ vertices i → v ∉ S
  /-- Every undeleted vertex belongs to exactly one part. -/
  unique : ∀ v, v ∉ S → ∃! i, v ∈ vertices i
  /-- No undeleted edge leaves a part. -/
  closed : ∀ i u v, u ∈ vertices i → v ∉ S → G.Adj u v → v ∈ vertices i

/-- Connected components of the induced graph give the canonical partition. -/
noncomputable def components {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (S : Finset (Fin n)) :
    Partition G S (G.induce (↑S : Set (Fin n))ᶜ).ConnectedComponent := by
  classical
  let H := G.induce (↑S : Set (Fin n))ᶜ
  let vertices (c : H.ConnectedComponent) := (Subtype.val '' c.supp).toFinset
  exact
    { vertices := vertices
      outside := by
        intro c v hv
        obtain ⟨u, _, rfl⟩ := Set.mem_toFinset.mp hv
        exact u.property
      unique := by
        intro v hv
        let u : ↥((↑S : Set (Fin n))ᶜ) := ⟨v, hv⟩
        refine ⟨H.connectedComponentMk u, ?_, ?_⟩
        · exact Set.mem_toFinset.mpr ⟨u, rfl, rfl⟩
        · intro c hc
          obtain ⟨w, hw, he⟩ := Set.mem_toFinset.mp hc
          have hwu : w = u := Subtype.ext he
          change H.connectedComponentMk w = c at hw
          rw [hwu] at hw
          exact hw.symm
      closed := by
        intro c u v hu hv huv
        obtain ⟨u', hu', rfl⟩ := Set.mem_toFinset.mp hu
        let v' : ↥((↑S : Set (Fin n))ᶜ) := ⟨v, hv⟩
        exact Set.mem_toFinset.mpr ⟨v',
          (SimpleGraph.ConnectedComponent.mem_supp_congr_adj c
            (show H.Adj u' v' from huv)).mp hu', rfl⟩ }

/-- The recursive answer is the union of the answers on the parts. -/
def combine {n : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (I : ι → Finset (Fin n)) :
    Finset (Fin n) := Finset.univ.biUnion I

end Lax263307.SeparatorComponents

concepts.title: Tree decompositions from recursive balanced separators
concepts.description:
Attach the decompositions of the parts below a new root bag containing the
separator, and add the separator to every child bag. The resulting bags have
size at most the separator size plus the largest child bag. Recursing on
balanced parts costs at most one separator bound per recursion level.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The component trees may have different finite node types. The joining tree
uses a disjoint dependent sum of these types and one additional root. The
recursive bound keeps its logarithmic depth explicit; conversion to an
edge-only sublinear bound is a separate step.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.SeparatorComponents
import Lax263307.EdgeSublinearSeparators
import Lax263307.RecursionDepth
import Lax228581.Treewidth

/-!
---
title: Tree decompositions from recursive balanced separators
type: theorem
---
Attach the decompositions of the parts below a new root bag containing the
separator, and add the separator to every child bag. The resulting bags have
size at most the separator size plus the largest child bag. Recursing on
balanced parts costs at most one separator bound per recursion level.

# Formalization notes

The component trees may have different finite node types. The joining tree
uses a disjoint dependent sum of these types and one additional root. The
recursive bound keeps its logarithmic depth explicit; conversion to an
edge-only sublinear bound is a separate step.
-/

namespace Lax263307.SeparatorDecompositions

open GraphClasses EdgeSublinearSeparators SeparatorComponents Lax228581.Treewidth

/-- Join the component decompositions below a separator root. -/
axiom glue_bound {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (S : Finset (Fin n))
    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (P : Partition G S ι)
    (D : ∀ i, TreeDecomposition (G.induce (↑(P.vertices i) : Set (Fin n))))
    (B : ℕ) (bound : ∀ i j, ((D i).bag j).card ≤ B) :
    ∃ E : TreeDecomposition G, ∀ j, (E.bag j).card ≤ S.card + B

/-- Balanced recursive separators give a logarithmic depth bag bound. -/
axiom recursive_bag_bound (C : GraphClass) (hereditary : IsHereditary C)
    (B : ℕ → ℕ) (monotone : Monotone B) (positive : ∀ m, 1 ≤ B m)
    (separators : ∀ n (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G ∈ C n →
      ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), IsBalancedSeparator G S ∧ S.card ≤ B G.edgeSet.ncard)
    {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (member : G ∈ C n) :
    ∃ D : TreeDecomposition G, ∀ j,
      (D.bag j).card ≤ B G.edgeSet.ncard * (RecursionDepth.depth n + 1)

end Lax263307.SeparatorDecompositions

  (P : Lax263307.SeparatorComponents.Partition G S ι)
  (D : (i : ι) → Lax228581.Treewidth.TreeDecomposition (SimpleGraph.induce (Finset.instSetLike.coe (P.vertices i)) G))
  (B : Nat),
  (∀ (i : ι) (j : (D i).Node), instLENat.le ((D i).bag j).card B) →
    Exists fun E => ∀ (j : E.Node), instLENat.le (E.bag j).card (instHAdd.hAdd S.card B)
