concepts.title: Controlled-size subcubic source graphs of linear treewidth
concepts.description:
The registered deterministic subcubic family supplies fixed positive
constants for width and size overshoot. For every requested order, choose a
source graph above the request and below a fixed multiple of the request
plus one, with order bounded by the width constant times treewidth plus one.
The upper size bound is needed to meet the route-sampling budgets.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown:
Lax920634's registered subcubic construction, size bound, and explicit
linear-treewidth theorem; the source family used in Bonnet–Chang, Lemma 10.

import Lax920634.ConstructionSize
import Lax920634.SubcubicConstruction
import Lax920634.ExplicitTreewidth

/-!
---
title: Controlled-size subcubic source graphs of linear treewidth
type: theorem
---
The registered deterministic subcubic family supplies fixed positive
constants for width and size overshoot. For every requested order, choose a
source graph above the request and below a fixed multiple of the request
plus one, with order bounded by the width constant times treewidth plus one.
The upper size bound is needed to meet the route-sampling budgets.

# Attribution

Lax920634's registered subcubic construction, size bound, and explicit
linear-treewidth theorem; the source family used in Bonnet–Chang, Lemma 10.
-/

namespace Lax263307.SourceGraphs

open Lax920634.ZigZagConstruction Lax920634.GraphEncoding Lax920634.SeedSearch
open Lax920634.EdgeExpansion Lax228581.Treewidth

axiom controlled_family : ∃ widthConstant sizeConstant : ℕ,
    0 < widthConstant ∧ 0 < sizeConstant ∧
    ∀ request : ℕ, ∃ n, ∃ H : SimpleGraph (Fin n), request ≤ n ∧
      n ≤ sizeConstant * (request + 1) ∧ IsSubcubic H ∧
      n ≤ widthConstant * (treewidth H + 1)

end Lax263307.SourceGraphs

  Exists fun sizeConstant =>
    And (instLTNat.lt 0 widthConstant)
      (And (instLTNat.lt 0 sizeConstant)
        (∀ (request : Nat),
          Exists fun n =>
            Exists fun H =>
              And (instLENat.le request n)
                (And (instLENat.le n (instHMul.hMul sizeConstant (instHAdd.hAdd request 1)))
                  (And (Lax920634.EdgeExpansion.IsSubcubic H)
                    (instLENat.le n
                      (instHMul.hMul widthConstant (instHAdd.hAdd (Lax228581.Treewidth.treewidth H) 1)))))))

concepts.title: Projecting split paths and preserving endpoint loads
concepts.description:
A simple path of positive-capacity arcs in the split network, starting at
$u^-$ and ending at $v^+$, is the expansion of a simple original path from
$u$ to $v$. Each original vertex expands to its consecutive input/output
ports. A reverse port arc would repeat an input port, so simplicity excludes
it. Successive original vertices must therefore be graph neighbors.

For a simple original route $Q$, the expanded route traverses the capacity
arc $w^-\to w^+$ exactly once when $w$ belongs to $Q$, and zero times
otherwise. This counts both endpoints and includes singleton routes.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown:
Bonnet–Chang, flow projection and endpoint-inclusive load accounting in
Lemma 7.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.VertexSplitting
import Mathlib.Data.List.Chain

/-!
---
title: Projecting split paths and preserving endpoint loads
type: theorem
---
A simple path of positive-capacity arcs in the split network, starting at
$u^-$ and ending at $v^+$, is the expansion of a simple original path from
$u$ to $v$. Each original vertex expands to its consecutive input/output
ports. A reverse port arc would repeat an input port, so simplicity excludes
it. Successive original vertices must therefore be graph neighbors.

For a simple original route $Q$, the expanded route traverses the capacity
arc $w^-\to w^+$ exactly once when $w$ belongs to $Q$, and zero times
otherwise. This counts both endpoints and includes singleton routes.

# Attribution

Bonnet–Chang, flow projection and endpoint-inclusive load accounting in
Lemma 7.
-/

namespace Lax263307.SplitPathProjection

open scoped NNReal NNRat
open VertexSplitting Lax455465.ProductNetwork Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow

/-- Replace each original route vertex by its consecutive two split ports. -/
def expandRoute {n : ℕ} (Q : List (Fin n)) : List (Fin (2 * n)) :=
  Q.flatMap fun v => [minus v, plus v]

/-- A positive simple split path projects to a simple original route. -/
axiom project_simple_path {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (x : Fin n → ℚ≥0) (large : ℚ≥0) (P : List (Fin (2 * n))) (u v : Fin n)
    (simple : P.Nodup)
    (chain : P.IsChain (fun a b => 0 < (splitInstance G x large).capacity a b))
    (start : P.head? = some (minus u)) (finish : P.getLast? = some (plus v)) :
    ∃ Q : List (Fin n), P = expandRoute Q ∧ Q.Nodup ∧ Q.IsChain G.Adj ∧
      Q.head? = some u ∧ Q.getLast? = some v

/-- Capacity-arc occurrence equals the original vertex-membership indicator. -/
axiom capacity_arc_count {n : ℕ} (Q : List (Fin n)) (simple : Q.Nodup) (v : Fin n) :
    ((expandRoute Q).zip (expandRoute Q).tail).count (minus v, plus v) =
      if v ∈ Q then 1 else 0

/-- Every retained positive path in a feasible split flow has such a projection. -/
axiom split_support_projection {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (x : Fin n → ℚ≥0) (large : ℚ≥0) (f : ℝ≥0) (F : PathFlow (2 * n))
    (feasible : IsConcurrentFlow .directed (splitInstance G x large).network
      (splitInstance G x large).weights f F)
    (P : List (Fin (2 * n))) (member : P ∈ F.support) (u v : Fin n)
    (start : P.head? = some (minus u)) (finish : P.getLast? = some (plus v)) :
    ∃ Q : List (Fin n), P = expandRoute Q ∧ Q.Nodup ∧ Q.IsChain G.Adj ∧
      Q.head? = some u ∧ Q.getLast? = some v

end Lax263307.SplitPathProjection

          ((Lax263307.SplitPathProjection.expandRoute Q).zip (Lax263307.SplitPathProjection.expandRoute Q).tail))

concepts.title: Quantitative gaps for recursive component cuts
concepts.description:
The collected component normal has sum of absolute coefficients at most
|C|+u, hence at most 2n for u≤n. A heavy part of conditioned cost at least
delta*k/(2n), queried at floor((1-delta)*cost)+1, gives a feasible-point
cut gap at least eta*delta²*k/(2n) whenever the conditioning moment is
at least eta>0. Nearby queried centers retain a positive gap.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The coordinate error radius eta*delta²/(8n²) leaves a query gap of at
least eta*delta²/(4n). A central cut with gap Delta retains an entire
coordinate cube of radius Delta/(4n) around every valid hull point.
This is the buffer needed for ellipsoid stopping even when the exact
independent-set hull has no ambient interior.

import Lax263307.ComponentCutEncoding

/-!
---
title: Quantitative gaps for recursive component cuts
type: theorem
---
The collected component normal has sum of absolute coefficients at most
|C|+u, hence at most 2n for u≤n. A heavy part of conditioned cost at least
delta*k/(2n), queried at floor((1-delta)*cost)+1, gives a feasible-point
cut gap at least eta*delta²*k/(2n) whenever the conditioning moment is
at least eta>0. Nearby queried centers retain a positive gap.

# Formalization notes

The coordinate error radius eta*delta²/(8n²) leaves a query gap of at
least eta*delta²/(4n). A central cut with gap Delta retains an entire
coordinate cube of radius Delta/(4n) around every valid hull point.
This is the buffer needed for ellipsoid stopping even when the exact
independent-set hull has no ambient interior.
-/

namespace Lax263307.StrongComponentGaps

open LinearRelaxation ComponentCutEncoding

axiom coefficient_l1 {n r : ℕ} (A C : Finset (Fin n)) (u : ℕ) :
    (∑ B : Coordinate n r, |(coefficient A C u B : ℝ)|) ≤ C.card + u

axiom evaluation_stable {n r : ℕ} (A C : Finset (Fin n)) (u : ℕ)
    (x y : MomentVector n r) (ρ : ℝ) (hρ : 0 ≤ ρ)
    (near : ∀ B, |x B - y B| ≤ ρ) :
    |evaluate (coefficient A C u) x - evaluate (coefficient A C u) y| ≤ (C.card + u) * ρ

axiom component_gap {n r : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (k : ℕ)
    (y : MomentVector n r) (A C : Finset (Fin n)) (u : ℕ)
    (size : A.card ≤ r) (bound : IsIndependenceBound G C u)
    (η δ : ℝ) (hη : 0 < η) (hδ : 0 < δ) (hn : 0 < n) (hk : 0 < k)
    (moment : η ≤ value y A)
    (heavy : δ * (k : ℝ) / (2 * n) ≤ ∑ v ∈ C, conditioned y A v)
    (rounded : (u : ℝ) ≤ (1 - δ) * ∑ v ∈ C, conditioned y A v) :
    (∀ z ∈ independentSetHull G k r, evaluate (coefficient A C u) z ≤ 0) ∧
      η * δ ^ 2 * (k : ℝ) / (2 * n) ≤ evaluate (coefficient A C u) y

axiom query_gap {n r : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (k : ℕ)
    (x y : MomentVector n r) (A C : Finset (Fin n)) (u : ℕ)
    (size : A.card ≤ r) (bound : IsIndependenceBound G C u) (upper : u ≤ n)
    (η δ : ℝ) (hη : 0 < η) (hδ : 0 < δ) (hn : 0 < n) (hk : 0 < k)
    (moment : η ≤ value y A)
    (heavy : δ * (k : ℝ) / (2 * n) ≤ ∑ v ∈ C, conditioned y A v)
    (rounded : (u : ℝ) ≤ (1 - δ) * ∑ v ∈ C, conditioned y A v)
    (near : ∀ B, |x B - y B| ≤ η * δ ^ 2 / (8 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2)) :
    (∀ z ∈ independentSetHull G k r, evaluate (coefficient A C u) z ≤ 0) ∧
      η * δ ^ 2 / (4 * n) ≤ evaluate (coefficient A C u) x

axiom central_cut_buffer {n r : ℕ} (A C : Finset (Fin n)) (u : ℕ) (upper : u ≤ n)
    (x z : MomentVector n r) (Δ : ℝ) (positive : 0 < Δ) (hn : 0 < n)
    (valid : evaluate (coefficient A C u) z ≤ 0)
    (gap : Δ ≤ evaluate (coefficient A C u) x)
    (perturbed : MomentVector n r)
    (near : ∀ B, |perturbed B - z B| ≤ Δ / (4 * n)) :
    evaluate (coefficient A C u) perturbed ≤ evaluate (coefficient A C u) x - Δ / 2

end Lax263307.StrongComponentGaps

                                  (Lax263307.ComponentCutEncoding.evaluate
                                    (Lax263307.ComponentCutEncoding.coefficient A C u) z)
                                  0)
                            (Real.instLE.le
                              (instHDiv.hDiv (instHMul.hMul η (instHPow.hPow δ 2)) (instHMul.hMul 4 n.cast))
                              (Lax263307.ComponentCutEncoding.evaluate
                                (Lax263307.ComponentCutEncoding.coefficient A C u) x))

concepts.title: Descending target search in Solve
concepts.description:
`Solve` tries targets in descending order. A failed target $k$ is accompanied
by a proof that every independent set has size less than $k$. A successful
target returns an independent set of size at least $\rho k$.
The first successful target is therefore a certified upper bound on the
independence number, and the returned set retains the factor $\rho$ of that
bound. The zero target provides the terminating empty-set case.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.LinearRelaxation
import Mathlib.Data.Rat.Defs

/-!
---
title: Descending target search in Solve
type: theorem
---
`Solve` tries targets in descending order. A failed target $k$ is accompanied
by a proof that every independent set has size less than $k$. A successful
target returns an independent set of size at least $\rho k$.
The first successful target is therefore a certified upper bound on the
independence number, and the returned set retains the factor $\rho$ of that
bound. The zero target provides the terminating empty-set case.

# Attribution

Bonnet–Chang, Algorithm 1 and the last paragraph of the proof of Lemma 14.
-/

namespace Lax263307.TargetSearch

/-- Try positive targets in decreasing order, falling back to the empty set. -/
def search {n : ℕ} (attempt : ℕ → Option (Finset (Fin n))) :
    ℕ → Finset (Fin n) × ℕ
  | 0 => (∅, 0)
  | k + 1 => match attempt (k + 1) with
    | some I => (I, k + 1)
    | none => search attempt k

/-- The target loop preserves the upper-bound and approximation invariants. -/
axiom search_correct {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (ρ : ℝ)
    (attempt : ℕ → Option (Finset (Fin n)))
    (success : ∀ k, k ≤ n → ∀ I, attempt k = some I →
      G.IsIndepSet (I : Set (Fin n)) ∧ ρ * k ≤ I.card)
    (failure : ∀ k, 0 < k → k ≤ n → attempt k = none →
      ∀ J : Finset (Fin n), G.IsIndepSet (J : Set (Fin n)) → J.card < k) :
    let result := search attempt n
    G.IsIndepSet (result.1 : Set (Fin n)) ∧
      (∀ J : Finset (Fin n), G.IsIndepSet (J : Set (Fin n)) → J.card ≤ result.2) ∧
      result.2 ≤ n ∧ ρ * result.2 ≤ result.1.card

end Lax263307.TargetSearch

  (∀ (k : Nat),
      instLENat.le k n →
        ∀ (I : Finset (Fin n)),
          Eq (attempt k) (Option.some I) →
            And (G.IsIndepSet (Finset.instSetLike.coe I)) (Real.instLE.le (instHMul.hMul ρ k.cast) I.card.cast)) →
    (∀ (k : Nat),
        instLTNat.lt 0 k →
          instLENat.le k n →
            Eq (attempt k) Option.none →
              ∀ (J : Finset (Fin n)), G.IsIndepSet (Finset.instSetLike.coe J) → instLTNat.lt J.card k) →
      let result := Lax263307.TargetSearch.search attempt n;
      And (G.IsIndepSet (Finset.instSetLike.coe result.fst))
        (And (∀ (J : Finset (Fin n)), G.IsIndepSet (Finset.instSetLike.coe J) → instLENat.le J.card result.snd)
          (And (instLENat.le result.snd n) (Real.instLE.le (instHMul.hMul ρ result.snd.cast) result.fst.card.cast)))

concepts.title: Vertex splitting for the directed flow–cut algorithm
concepts.description:
Replace each original vertex $v$ by two ports $v^-$ and $v^+$.
The capacity of $v^-\to v^+$ is its cost $x_v$. Reverse port arcs and arcs
$v^+\to u^-$ for graph edges receive a sufficiently large finite capacity.
A directed cut of capacity less than this large capacity crosses none of
these arcs and projects to a separation of the original graph. Its capacity
equals the vertex cost of the projected separator.

The registered directed uniform flow–cut algorithm applies to this rational
split network with its actual RAM polynomial-time guarantee. Each original
ordered pair uses the distinct split endpoints $u^-,v^+$, also when $u=v$.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Ports are numbered $2v$ and $2v+1$. The cut shores are the vertices whose
minus ports lie inside the cut and whose plus ports lie outside it.
The cut projection and the external solver's application are proved here;
flow projection and the RAM cost of constructing the split input are separate
steps of the reduction.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown:
Bonnet–Chang, the vertex-splitting reduction in Lemma 7, using the registered
Leighton–Rao algorithm in Lax455465.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax455465.RamDirectedUniformFlowCut
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite
import Mathlib.Tactic

/-!
---
title: Vertex splitting for the directed flow–cut algorithm
type: theorem
---
Replace each original vertex $v$ by two ports $v^-$ and $v^+$.
The capacity of $v^-\to v^+$ is its cost $x_v$. Reverse port arcs and arcs
$v^+\to u^-$ for graph edges receive a sufficiently large finite capacity.
A directed cut of capacity less than this large capacity crosses none of
these arcs and projects to a separation of the original graph. Its capacity
equals the vertex cost of the projected separator.

The registered directed uniform flow–cut algorithm applies to this rational
split network with its actual RAM polynomial-time guarantee. Each original
ordered pair uses the distinct split endpoints $u^-,v^+$, also when $u=v$.

# Formalization notes

Ports are numbered $2v$ and $2v+1$. The cut shores are the vertices whose
minus ports lie inside the cut and whose plus ports lie outside it.
The cut projection and the external solver's application are proved here;
flow projection and the RAM cost of constructing the split input are separate
steps of the reduction.

# Attribution

Bonnet–Chang, the vertex-splitting reduction in Lemma 7, using the registered
Leighton–Rao algorithm in Lax455465.
-/

namespace Lax263307.VertexSplitting

open scoped NNReal NNRat
open Lax455465.RationalEncoding Lax455465.ProductNetwork Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow

/-- The input port of an original vertex. -/
def minus {n : ℕ} (v : Fin n) : Fin (2 * n) := ⟨2 * v.val, by omega⟩
/-- The output port of an original vertex. -/
def plus {n : ℕ} (v : Fin n) : Fin (2 * n) := ⟨2 * v.val + 1, by omega⟩
/-- Forget which of the two ports represents a vertex. -/
def original {n : ℕ} (v : Fin (2 * n)) : Fin n := ⟨v.val / 2, by omega⟩

/-- Rational capacities and uniform demands on the split network. -/
def splitInstance {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (x : Fin n → ℚ≥0) (large : ℚ≥0) : RationalInstance (2 * n) where
  capacity u v :=
    if u.val % 2 = 0 ∧ v.val = u.val + 1 then x (original u)
    else if u.val % 2 = 1 ∧ v.val + 1 = u.val then large
    else if u.val % 2 = 1 ∧ v.val % 2 = 0 ∧ G.Adj (original u) (original v) then large
    else 0
  loopless v := by
    have hforward : ¬(v.val % 2 = 0 ∧ v.val = v.val + 1) := by omega
    have hreverse : ¬(v.val % 2 = 1 ∧ v.val + 1 = v.val) := by omega
    have hedge : ¬(v.val % 2 = 1 ∧ v.val % 2 = 0 ∧ G.Adj (original v) (original v)) := by omega
    simp only [if_neg hforward, if_neg hreverse, if_neg hedge]
  weight _ := 1

/-- Original vertices whose input ports lie inside the split cut. -/
def leftShore {n : ℕ} (U : Finset (Fin (2 * n))) : Finset (Fin n) :=
  Finset.univ.filter fun v => minus v ∈ U

/-- Original vertices whose output ports lie outside the split cut. -/
def rightShore {n : ℕ} (U : Finset (Fin (2 * n))) : Finset (Fin n) :=
  Finset.univ.filter fun v => plus v ∉ U

/-- A small split cut projects to a nontrivial separation with controlled shores. -/
axiom small_cut_separation {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (x : Fin n → ℚ≥0) (large : ℚ≥0) (U : Finset (Fin (2 * n)))
    (small : cutCapacity (splitInstance G x large).network U < (large : ℝ≥0))
    (nonempty : U.Nonempty) (proper : Uᶜ.Nonempty) :
    (leftShore U).Nonempty ∧ (rightShore U).Nonempty ∧
      leftShore U ∪ rightShore U = Finset.univ ∧
      (∀ u ∈ leftShore U \ rightShore U, ∀ v ∈ rightShore U \ leftShore U, ¬G.Adj u v) ∧
      U.card ≤ 2 * (leftShore U).card ∧ Uᶜ.card ≤ 2 * (rightShore U).card

/-- Only the vertex-capacity arcs contribute to a small split cut. -/
axiom small_cut_cost {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (x : Fin n → ℚ≥0) (large : ℚ≥0) (U : Finset (Fin (2 * n)))
    (small : cutCapacity (splitInstance G x large).network U < (large : ℝ≥0)) :
    cutCapacity (splitInstance G x large).network U =
      ∑ v ∈ leftShore U ∩ rightShore U, (x v : ℝ≥0)

/-- Translate a directed cut ratio into the original separator's vertex cost. -/
axiom separator_cost_bound {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (x : Fin n → ℚ≥0) (large : ℚ≥0) (U : Finset (Fin (2 * n))) (ρ : ℝ)
    (nonnegative : 0 ≤ ρ)
    (small : cutCapacity (splitInstance G x large).network U < (large : ℝ≥0))
    (admissible : AdmissibleCut (splitInstance G x large).weights U)
    (ratio : (ratioCost (splitInstance G x large).network
      (splitInstance G x large).weights U : ℝ) ≤ ρ) :
    (∑ v ∈ leftShore U ∩ rightShore U, (x v : ℝ)) ≤
      4 * ρ * (leftShore U).card * (rightShore U).card

/-- Apply the existing directed uniform solver to every split network. -/
axiom split_certificate :
  ∃ (solve : List ℕ → List ℕ) (C : ℝ), Lax759944.RamPolytime.RamPolytime solve ∧ 0 < C ∧
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
      (x : Fin n → ℚ≥0) (large : ℚ≥0), 0 < n →
      let I := splitInstance G x large
      ∃ certificate : Lax455465.FlowCutCertificate.Certificate (2 * n),
        solve (encodeInput .directed I) = Lax455465.FlowCutCertificate.encodeCertificate certificate ∧
        AdmissibleCut I.weights certificate.cut ∧
        IsArcConcurrentFlow .directed I.network I.weights
          (certificate.flow.value : ℝ≥0) certificate.flow.flow ∧
        (ratioCost I.network I.weights certificate.cut : ℝ) ≤
          C * logFactor (2 * n) * (certificate.flow.value : ℝ)

/-- A split flow–cut certificate yields a high-value flow or a cheap separation. -/
axiom flow_or_separation {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (x : Fin n → ℚ≥0) (large : ℚ≥0)
    (certificate : Lax455465.FlowCutCertificate.Certificate (2 * n)) (ρ γ : ℝ)
    (nonnegative : 0 ≤ ρ) (positive : 0 < γ)
    (admissible : AdmissibleCut (splitInstance G x large).weights certificate.cut)
    (flow_valid : IsArcConcurrentFlow .directed (splitInstance G x large).network
      (splitInstance G x large).weights (certificate.flow.value : ℝ≥0) certificate.flow.flow)
    (ratio : (ratioCost (splitInstance G x large).network
      (splitInstance G x large).weights certificate.cut : ℝ) ≤
        ρ * (certificate.flow.value : ℝ))
    (large_capacity : ρ * (2 * n : ℕ) ^ 2 / γ < (large : ℝ)) :
    ((1 / γ ≤ (certificate.flow.value : ℝ)) ∧
      IsArcConcurrentFlow .directed (splitInstance G x large).network
        (splitInstance G x large).weights (certificate.flow.value : ℝ≥0) certificate.flow.flow) ∨
    ((leftShore certificate.cut).Nonempty ∧ (rightShore certificate.cut).Nonempty ∧
      leftShore certificate.cut ∪ rightShore certificate.cut = Finset.univ ∧
      (∀ u ∈ leftShore certificate.cut \ rightShore certificate.cut,
        ∀ v ∈ rightShore certificate.cut \ leftShore certificate.cut, ¬G.Adj u v) ∧
      (∑ v ∈ leftShore certificate.cut ∩ rightShore certificate.cut, (x v : ℝ)) ≤
        4 * ρ * (leftShore certificate.cut).card * (rightShore certificate.cut).card / γ)

end Lax263307.VertexSplitting

concepts.title: Correctness of the complete weighted approximation algorithm
concepts.description:
Clip negative weights, round them to copy multiplicities, and compute the
unweighted approximation on the canonically numbered independent blow-up.
Projection and removal of nonpositive-weight vertices give the requested
weighted approximation. Empty and nonpositive instances return the empty set.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The algorithm is a computable function using the fixed registered LP and
flow solvers. The copy labeling is the computable finite-sigma equivalence.
This closes functional correctness for signed rational weights, including
the recursive search. It does not yet assert a complete RAM execution or
its quasipolynomial time and word-length bounds.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.RecursiveAlgorithm
import Lax263307.BlowUpBagBounds
import Lax263307.PositiveWeights
import Lax263307.WeightedProjection
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin

/-!
---
title: Correctness of the complete weighted approximation algorithm
type: theorem
---
Clip negative weights, round them to copy multiplicities, and compute the
unweighted approximation on the canonically numbered independent blow-up.
Projection and removal of nonpositive-weight vertices give the requested
weighted approximation. Empty and nonpositive instances return the empty set.

# Formalization notes

The algorithm is a computable function using the fixed registered LP and
flow solvers. The copy labeling is the computable finite-sigma equivalence.
This closes functional correctness for signed rational weights, including
the recursive search. It does not yet assert a complete RAM execution or
its quasipolynomial time and word-length bounds.
-/

namespace Lax263307.WeightedAlgorithm

open WeightRounding IndependentBlowUp PositiveWeights

def labeling {n : ℕ} (copies : Fin n → ℕ) : Fin (∑ v, copies v) ≃ Vertex copies :=
  finSigmaFinEquiv.symm

def numbered {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (copies : Fin n → ℕ) :
    SimpleGraph (Fin (∑ v, copies v)) := (graph G copies).comap (labeling copies)

instance {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (copies : Fin n → ℕ) :
    DecidableRel (numbered G copies).Adj := fun _ _ => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (G.Adj _ _))

def solve {n : ℕ} (lp flow : List ℕ → List ℕ) (a K B : ℕ)
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (w : Fin n → ℚ) (ε : ℚ) : Finset (Fin n) :=
  let w' := positiveWeights w
  if n = 0 ∨ maximumWeight w' ≤ 0 then ∅
  else
    let copies' := copies w' ε
    let I := RecursiveAlgorithm.independentSet lp flow a K B (numbered G copies') (ε/2)
    discardNonpositive w (project (I.image (labeling copies')))

open GraphClasses EdgeSublinearSeparators WeightedIndependentSet

axiom exists_solver (C : GraphClass) (hereditary : IsHereditary C)
    (separators : HasStronglyEdgeSublinearSeparators C) :
    ∃ (lp flow : List ℕ → List ℕ) (a K B : ℕ),
      Lax759944.RamPolytime.RamPolytime lp ∧ Lax759944.RamPolytime.RamPolytime flow ∧
      0 < a ∧ 0 < K ∧ 0 < B ∧
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj], G ∈ C n →
      ∀ (w : Fin n → ℚ) (ε : ℚ), 0 < ε → ε < 1 → IsApproximation G w ε (solve lp flow a K B G w ε)

end Lax263307.WeightedAlgorithm

  Lax263307.GraphClasses.IsHereditary C →
    Lax263307.EdgeSublinearSeparators.HasStronglyEdgeSublinearSeparators C →
      Exists fun lp =>
        Exists fun flow =>
          Exists fun a =>
            Exists fun K =>
              Exists fun B =>
                And (Lax759944.RamPolytime.RamPolytime lp)
                  (And (Lax759944.RamPolytime.RamPolytime flow)
                    (And (instLTNat.lt 0 a)
                      (And (instLTNat.lt 0 K)
                        (And (instLTNat.lt 0 B)
                          (∀ (n : Nat) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [inst : DecidableRel G.Adj],
                            Set.instMembership.mem (C n) G →
                              ∀ (w : Fin n → Rat) (ε : Rat),
                                Rat.instLT.lt 0 ε →
                                  Rat.instLT.lt ε 1 →
                                    Lax263307.WeightedIndependentSet.IsApproximation G w ε
                                      (Lax263307.WeightedAlgorithm.solve lp flow a K B G w ε))))))

concepts.title: Maximum-weight independent set and its encoding
concepts.description:
Given a graph $G$ with rational vertex weights $w$, maximum-weight
independent set asks for an independent set of maximum total weight.
An $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation is an independent set $I$ with
$w(I)\ge(1-\varepsilon)w(J)$ for every independent set $J$.

The input consists of the number of vertices, the adjacency matrix,
the vertex weights, and the requested rational accuracy. The output
is the membership vector of the returned independent set.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The comparison with every independent set avoids choosing an optimum.
Weights may be negative: such vertices can be discarded, as can zero-weight
vertices, so this includes the nonnegative case used in Section 6.
Each rational is encoded by the sign of its reduced numerator, its absolute
numerator, and its positive denominator. The sign is zero for nonnegative
numbers and one for negative numbers. All matrix and vector entries are in
vertex order. The rational encoding length $\ell$ includes the weights and
$\varepsilon$, and is measured by the registered binary word encoding.

concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Clique
import Mathlib.Data.Rat.Floor
import Lax759944.BinaryWordEncoding

/-!
---
title: Maximum-weight independent set and its encoding
type: definition
---
Given a graph $G$ with rational vertex weights $w$, maximum-weight
independent set asks for an independent set of maximum total weight.
An $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation is an independent set $I$ with
$w(I)\ge(1-\varepsilon)w(J)$ for every independent set $J$.

The input consists of the number of vertices, the adjacency matrix,
the vertex weights, and the requested rational accuracy. The output
is the membership vector of the returned independent set.

# Formalization notes

The comparison with every independent set avoids choosing an optimum.
Weights may be negative: such vertices can be discarded, as can zero-weight
vertices, so this includes the nonnegative case used in Section 6.
Each rational is encoded by the sign of its reduced numerator, its absolute
numerator, and its positive denominator. The sign is zero for nonnegative
numbers and one for negative numbers. All matrix and vector entries are in
vertex order. The rational encoding length $\ell$ includes the weights and
$\varepsilon$, and is measured by the registered binary word encoding.
-/

namespace Lax263307.WeightedIndependentSet

/-- Total weight of a vertex set. -/
def weight {n : ℕ} (w : Fin n → ℚ) (I : Finset (Fin n)) : ℚ :=
  ∑ v ∈ I, w v

/-- An independent set that achieves the requested multiplicative guarantee. -/
def IsApproximation {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (w : Fin n → ℚ)
    (ε : ℚ) (I : Finset (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  G.IsIndepSet (I : Set (Fin n)) ∧
    ∀ J : Finset (Fin n), G.IsIndepSet (J : Set (Fin n)) →
      (1 - ε) * weight w J ≤ weight w I

/-- Canonical sign, absolute numerator, and denominator of a rational. -/
def encodeRational (q : ℚ) : List ℕ :=
  [if q.num < 0 then 1 else 0, q.num.natAbs, q.den]

/-- The rational parameters in vertex order, followed by the accuracy. -/
def encodeParameters {n : ℕ} (w : Fin n → ℚ) (ε : ℚ) : List ℕ :=
  (List.ofFn w).flatMap encodeRational ++ encodeRational ε

/-- Total binary encoding length of the weights and the accuracy. -/
def rationalBitSize {n : ℕ} (w : Fin n → ℚ) (ε : ℚ) : ℕ :=
  Lax759944.BinaryWordEncoding.bitSize (encodeParameters w ε)

/-- The full input word, including the row-major adjacency matrix. -/
def encodeInput {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (w : Fin n → ℚ) (ε : ℚ) : List ℕ :=
  [n] ++ (List.ofFn fun u => List.ofFn fun v =>
    if G.Adj u v then 1 else 0).flatten ++ encodeParameters w ε

/-- The length-`n` membership vector of the selected independent set. -/
def encodeOutput {n : ℕ} (I : Finset (Fin n)) : List ℕ :=
  List.ofFn fun v => if v ∈ I then 1 else 0

end Lax263307.WeightedIndependentSet

concepts.title: Projecting an unweighted approximation gives a weighted approximation
concepts.description:
Let an $n$-vertex graph have nonnegative rational weights, with positive
maximum weight $W$, and let $0<\varepsilon<1$.
Use multiplicities $t_v=\lfloor w_v/\tau\rfloor$, where
$\tau=\varepsilon W/(2n)$. A $(1-\varepsilon/2)$-approximate independent
set in the blow-up projects to a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximate weighted
independent set in the original graph.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown: Bonnet–Chang, the approximation guarantee in the proof of Theorem 2.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
This is the approximation transfer. Preservation of the graph-class
separator hypothesis under blow-ups and the algorithm's running time
are separate obligations.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.RoundingBounds
import Lax263307.BlowUpIndependentSets

/-!
---
title: Projecting an unweighted approximation gives a weighted approximation
type: theorem
---
Let an $n$-vertex graph have nonnegative rational weights, with positive
maximum weight $W$, and let $0<\varepsilon<1$.
Use multiplicities $t_v=\lfloor w_v/\tau\rfloor$, where
$\tau=\varepsilon W/(2n)$. A $(1-\varepsilon/2)$-approximate independent
set in the blow-up projects to a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximate weighted
independent set in the original graph.

# Attribution

Bonnet–Chang, the approximation guarantee in the proof of Theorem 2.

# Formalization notes

This is the approximation transfer. Preservation of the graph-class
separator hypothesis under blow-ups and the algorithm's running time
are separate obligations.
-/

namespace Lax263307.WeightedProjection

open WeightedIndependentSet WeightRounding IndependentBlowUp

/-- The two half-accuracy losses combine into the requested weighted guarantee. -/
axiom approximation_transfer {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (w : Fin n → ℚ)
    (ε : ℚ) (nonnegative : ∀ v, 0 ≤ w v) (positive_order : 0 < n)
    (positive_accuracy : 0 < ε) (accuracy_lt_one : ε < 1)
    (positive_maximum : 0 < maximumWeight w)
    (K : Finset (Vertex (copies w ε)))
    (approximation : IsCardinalityApproximation G (copies w ε) (ε / 2) K) :
    IsApproximation G w ε (project K)

end Lax263307.WeightedProjection

statements.signature:
approximation_transfer : ∀ {n : Nat} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (w : Fin n → Rat) (ε : Rat),
  (∀ (v : Fin n), Rat.instLE.le 0 (w v)) →
    instLTNat.lt 0 n →
      Rat.instLT.lt 0 ε →
        Rat.instLT.lt ε 1 →
          Rat.instLT.lt 0 (Lax263307.WeightRounding.maximumWeight w) →
            ∀ (K : Finset (Lax263307.IndependentBlowUp.Vertex (Lax263307.WeightRounding.copies w ε))),
              Lax263307.IndependentBlowUp.IsCardinalityApproximation G (Lax263307.WeightRounding.copies w ε)
                  (instHDiv.hDiv ε 2) K →
                Lax263307.WeightedIndependentSet.IsApproximation G w ε (Lax263307.IndependentBlowUp.project K)
statements.doc: The two half-accuracy losses combine into the requested weighted guarantee.

concepts.title: Scaling weights to integer multiplicities
concepts.description:
For nonnegative rational vertex weights, let $W$ be the maximum weight and
choose $\tau=\varepsilon W/(2n)$. The rounded multiplicity of vertex $v$ is
$t_v=\lfloor w_v/\tau\rfloor$. Vertices with $t_v=0$ are omitted from the
independent blow-up.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The maximum includes zero, so it is defined also on the empty graph and on
signed weights before preprocessing. The rounding estimates assume
$n>0$, $W>0$, and $\varepsilon>0$, ensuring $\tau>0$.
The natural-valued floor is computed on exact rational numbers.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.IndependentBlowUp
import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Max

/-!
---
title: Scaling weights to integer multiplicities
type: definition
---
For nonnegative rational vertex weights, let $W$ be the maximum weight and
choose $\tau=\varepsilon W/(2n)$. The rounded multiplicity of vertex $v$ is
$t_v=\lfloor w_v/\tau\rfloor$. Vertices with $t_v=0$ are omitted from the
independent blow-up.

# Formalization notes

The maximum includes zero, so it is defined also on the empty graph and on
signed weights before preprocessing. The rounding estimates assume
$n>0$, $W>0$, and $\varepsilon>0$, ensuring $\tau>0$.
The natural-valued floor is computed on exact rational numbers.
-/

namespace Lax263307.WeightRounding

/-- The maximum of the vertex weights and zero. -/
def maximumWeight {n : ℕ} (w : Fin n → ℚ) : ℚ :=
  (insert 0 (Finset.univ.image w)).max' (by simp)

/-- The weight unit used by the reduction. -/
def scale {n : ℕ} (w : Fin n → ℚ) (ε : ℚ) : ℚ :=
  ε * maximumWeight w / (2 * n)

/-- Multiplicities at a specified positive weight unit. -/
def roundedCopies {n : ℕ} (w : Fin n → ℚ) (τ : ℚ) : Fin n → ℕ :=
  fun v => ⌊w v / τ⌋₊

/-- The multiplicities chosen for the requested accuracy. -/
def copies {n : ℕ} (w : Fin n → ℚ) (ε : ℚ) : Fin n → ℕ :=
  roundedCopies w (scale w ε)

end Lax263307.WeightRounding

concepts.title: Polynomial order bound from the sampled width inequality
concepts.description:
Suppose $W(m)^a\le A(m+1)^{a-1}$ and $W(m)\ge1$. For a source graph of
order $t$ and at most $2t$ edges, take route cutoff $24c\ell$. If its linear
width lower bound and discarded-route estimate are both compatible with
the sampled width upper bound, then
$t\le (12c)^a A(6(24c)^2+1)^{a-1}\ell^{2(a-1)}$.
This integer inequality makes the sampling contradiction polynomial in ell.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown: The growth calculation in Bonnet–Chang, proof of Lemma 11.

concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Basic

/-!
---
title: Polynomial order bound from the sampled width inequality
type: theorem
---
Suppose $W(m)^a\le A(m+1)^{a-1}$ and $W(m)\ge1$. For a source graph of
order $t$ and at most $2t$ edges, take route cutoff $24c\ell$. If its linear
width lower bound and discarded-route estimate are both compatible with
the sampled width upper bound, then
$t\le (12c)^a A(6(24c)^2+1)^{a-1}\ell^{2(a-1)}$.
This integer inequality makes the sampling contradiction polynomial in ell.

# Attribution

The growth calculation in Bonnet–Chang, proof of Lemma 11.
-/

namespace Lax263307.WidthGrowth

def threshold (a A c : ℕ) : ℕ := (12 * c) ^ a * A * (6 * (24 * c) ^ 2 + 1) ^ (a - 1)

axiom order_bound (a A c ℓ t m q : ℕ) (a_positive : 0 < a) (ℓ_positive : 0 < ℓ)
    (t_positive : 0 < t) (W : ℕ → ℕ)
    (W_positive : ∀ M, 1 ≤ W M) (W_power : ∀ M, (W M) ^ a ≤ A * (M + 1) ^ (a - 1))
    (edges : m ≤ 2 * t) (discarded : (24 * c * ℓ) * q ≤ 4 * m * ℓ)
    (width : t ≤ c * (max 1 (6 * W (3 * m * (24 * c * ℓ) ^ 2)) + q)) :
    t ≤ threshold a A c * ℓ ^ (2 * (a - 1))

end Lax263307.WidthGrowth

statements.signature:
order_bound : ∀ (a A c ℓ t m q : Nat),
  instLTNat.lt 0 a →
    instLTNat.lt 0 ℓ →
      instLTNat.lt 0 t →
        ∀ (W : Nat → Nat),
          (∀ (M : Nat), instLENat.le 1 (W M)) →
            (∀ (M : Nat),
                instLENat.le (instHPow.hPow (W M) a)
                  (instHMul.hMul A (instHPow.hPow (instHAdd.hAdd M 1) (instHSub.hSub a 1)))) →
              instLENat.le m (instHMul.hMul 2 t) →
                instLENat.le (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul 24 c) ℓ) q)
                    (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul 4 m) ℓ) →
                  instLENat.le t
                      (instHMul.hMul c
                        (instHAdd.hAdd
                          (Nat.instMax.max 1
                            (instHMul.hMul 6
                              (W
                                (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul 3 m)
                                  (instHPow.hPow (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul 24 c) ℓ) 2)))))
                          q)) →
                    instLENat.le t
                      (instHMul.hMul (Lax263307.WidthGrowth.threshold a A c)
                        (instHPow.hPow ℓ (instHMul.hMul 2 (instHSub.hSub a 1))))

proofs.description:
The load clears the accuracy denominator exactly. Sparsity is twice the
target threshold, and the level is the sparsity times the binary-log bound.

The integer floor denominator is exactly the denominator of the heavy
conditioning probability floor; rational casts preserve its reciprocal power.

The protected-radius denominator is positive. A power of two with exponent
that denominator plus two is larger than the denominator itself.

Represent a vertex by the union of its incident routes, connected through
its mapped image. At a host vertex, all routes present share an endpoint
with any one present route `xy`; their endpoints lie in `N(x) ∪ N(y)`.
Thus at most `2d` represented vertices use that host vertex. Apply the
connected-set decomposition transfer with this load bound.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown: Bonnet–Chang, Lemma 9.

proofs.description:
Pick a vertex in each connected component and its unique partition part.
Every walk with undeleted vertices stays in that closed part, so the
component’s image is contained in it. Injective projection preserves the
component cardinality, which is bounded by the part size.

Raise the real sublinear blow-up bag bound to a fixed positive integer
power, absorb its constant into a positive integer, and dominate its
exponent by a-1 using a(1-beta)>1.

Restrict the base graph to used projection fibres, retaining class membership.
One representative per fibre embeds it into the given blow-up and bounds
its edge count. Enumerate the fibres to form an explicit copy-graph
isomorphism. Apply degree-deletion optimization to its base decomposition
and pull the resulting bags through that isomorphism.

Every explicitly constructed copy graph, relabeled to a numbered vertex
set, belongs to the independent blow-up closure.

sections.title: Proof strategy

Project each labeled copy to its original vertex. By definition of the
comap graph, adjacency is exactly adjacency of these original vertices.

The embedding and projection both preserve and reflect adjacency.

neighbor has degree at least that fibre size. Embed these survivors into the
uniform `s`-fold blow-up, pull back its lifted decomposition, insert the
isolated survivors in singleton bags, and add the removed vertices to every
bag.

the lifted-bag term then both have exponent `(1+b)/2`, with the additional

Copies of a common original vertex have no edge between them. For different

proofs.description: A single coordinate square is bounded by the sum of squares; take the nonnegative square root bound.
The squared norm of a sum is at most twice each summand square. Both the scaled cube point and the perturbation have squared norm at most 1/16.
A nonzero integer coordinate has squared magnitude at least one. Its square is bounded by the sum of all coordinate squares.
Each scaled coordinate lies between zero and 1/(4n). Sum the squared bounds and use n≥1.

The positive contribution counts at most `|C| ≤ n` terms, each equal to one.
The negative contribution is either zero or `u ≤ n`. Their difference lies
between `-n` and `n`, even when inserted coordinates repeat.

selects precisely its coordinate; the final term selects the coordinate of
the conditioning set.

The recursive independence bound yields an inequality valid throughout

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
On an indicator vector the left side is zero if the conditioning set is
absent, and otherwise equals the size of the intersection with `C`.
The upper bound applies to this independent intersection. The halfspace
is convex, so the inequality extends to the entire hull.

proofs.description:
Inspect the actual first failed query. Its certified independence bound and
rational target give the buffered component gap. If no query fails, skipped
parts contribute the empty set and the successful answers satisfy the proved

The fixed registered solver is called on canonically labeled remainders.
Its actual cut prefixes determine the entire bounded cut list. The resulting
computed parts are the vertices of the checked balanced partition.

Use the uniform endpoint mass and multiply by n². Positive conditional
weights have the prescribed endpoints and inherit route validity.

Factor the four finite endpoint sums into two separate sums and use
the mixture identity for each route. Cancel the factor n⁴.

Every positive-probability route is nonempty and has a unique ordered
endpoint pair. All other terms in the endpoint sum vanish.

Conditioning preserves the unit-interval bounds and total mass, fixes the
chosen vertices to one, and preserves positivity at every positive-cost step.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Divide the monotonicity inequalities and mass equation by the positive
conditioning moment. Inserting a vertex already in the conditioning set
does not change the set.

proofs.description:
The first and second conditioned moments define the probability
distributions used by the entropy argument.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
The mass equation at `A` normalizes the vertex distribution; the same
equation at `A ∪ {v}` gives the marginal of the joint distribution.
Symmetry is commutativity of insertion. A set containing the endpoints
of an edge has zero moment. Clearing positive denominators gives the
conditional-probability identity.

proofs.description:
The conditioning process reaches the required edge-cost threshold within
the available number of vertices.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Assume that every admissible small conditioning set exceeds the threshold.
Starting at the empty set, repeatedly apply the strict entropy-decrease
statement. After `r` steps the entropy would be strictly less than zero,
contradicting the entropy bounds. The resulting set inherits the checked
cost bounds and mass equation.

sections.markdown: Bonnet–Chang, proof of Lemma 12.

proofs.description:
Choose witnesses in the two bags and a walk joining them inside the connected
vertex set. For each edge of that walk, use a bag containing its endpoints.
The connected bag indices for each vertex join these edge bags into a walk
between the original nodes, entirely inside the nodes meeting the vertex set.

proofs.description:
Keep the original tree and replace each bag by all represented vertices
whose carriers meet it. Connected carriers preserve connected bag indices;
touching carriers ensure edge coverage. Sum the load bound over each original
bag to obtain the new bag-size bound.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown: The transfer construction in Bonnet–Chang, Lemma 9.

proofs.description: Duplicate removal cannot increase length. Apply the bounded-size candidate count at level r+2.
Candidate completeness and preservation of membership under duplicate removal list every coordinate.
Removing duplicates and injectively attaching each cardinality proof preserves distinctness.
The empty coordinate is always listed, so the catalog is nonempty.
For positive graph order, the empty coordinate and a singleton coordinate are distinct catalog members.

Apply the three cost-based sampling estimates. The target and sparsity
thresholds bound the two interaction contributions by 1/8 each. The
expected total route size is at most m*ell, which is positive. Invoke the
proved sampled width obstruction with this value of M.

For each fixed vertex assignment, conditional edge routes form a
normalized product law. Sum them out, then sum the uniform vertex law.

Positive joint probability forces positive conditional probability
for every edge. Conditional support fixes endpoints and gives simple
graph routes.

Sum out all other edge routes. Restrict the uniform vertex assignment
to the four distinct endpoints, then apply the independent endpoint
mixture identity.

First sum out all other edge routes. Restrict the uniform vertex
assignment to the two distinct edge endpoints, then use the conditional
mixture identity.

Apply the union bound over ordered source-edge pairs. Every nonincident
pair has the independent route law; its interaction probability is at
most collision plus adjacency probability. There are at most m² pairs.

Reindex the finite coupled outcome space by Fin and apply the proved
good-outcome lemma to the bad interaction event and total route size.
The probability and length estimates provide its two bounds.

Interchange the sums over outcomes and source edges, then use each
edge route’s marginal law to compute its expected size.

Induct on remainder cardinality. A large remainder receives an oracle
cut whose nonempty right shore strictly reduces it; prepend that cut to
the recursively constructed trace. A small remainder stops immediately.
Apply the proved trace analysis to obtain the final separator and cost.

The remainder equals the initial set minus previously discarded shores.
Hence discarded shores are disjoint and their nonemptiness bounds the
number of cuts. The exclusive pieces and final remainder partition all
undeleted vertices without cross edges. Their size bounds certify balance;
the cumulative cut-cost theorem gives the separator budget.

The distance column bounds the sum of the two nonnegative multiplier families by one. Their difference is therefore bounded in L1, and the original columns and rows make it valid on every feasible point.
The objective equals the negative of the nonnegative distance variable, hence is at most zero.
Combine primal characterization with the dual normal bounds. Matching objectives identify the separation gap at the center with the returned distance.
Expand the appended rows and split finite indices. The two distance inequalities are exactly the coordinate absolute-value bounds.
Every projected primal point gives an original feasible point. Conversely append the sum of coordinate absolute differences as a feasible distance bound.
Compare the returned distance with the chosen radius. The primal point is either within that radius, or the dual normal separates by strictly more than it.

Choose a positive integer a with a(1-beta)>1. Raise the sublinear bag
bound to its a-th power, enlarge the constant to a positive integer A,
and use a*beta≤a-1 and m+1≥1 to bound the remaining real power.

Round separator sizes up to a monotone positive integer bound, and recurse
on balanced components. Delete isolated vertices first so the recursive
order is at most twice the edge count, then restore their singleton bags.
The inequality log x ≤ x^epsilon/epsilon absorbs depth at exponent
beta=(1+b)/2, still below one.

Choose the first endpoint of each deleted unordered pair. Their image has
cardinality at most the number of deleted edges and meets every deleted edge.
Add this image to every bag, restoring coverage while preserving connected
bag indices. Bound each enlarged bag by the sum of its two constituent sizes.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown: The deletion estimate used in Bonnet–Chang, Lemma 11.

proofs.description:
The entropy of a probability vector lies between zero and the logarithm
of the number of vertices.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Each entropy summand is nonnegative. Jensen's inequality for the concave
function `negMulLog` bounds their sum by the entropy of the uniform vector.
Divide by the positive logarithm of two to obtain the bound in bits.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown: Bonnet–Chang, proof of Lemma 12.

proofs.description:
Exceeding the edge-cost threshold forces a positive-cost vertex whose
conditioning decreases entropy by more than the prescribed amount.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Normalize the costs by the target size and apply the average entropy-gap
inequality to the joint distribution. A strictly small weighted average
has a strictly small term with positive weight. The checked conditional
probability identities identify that term with the next conditioning step.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown: Bonnet–Chang, proof of Lemma 12, equation (18).

proofs.description:
The expected entropy decrease is at least the product probability of
ordered adjacent pairs.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
The entropy chain rule expresses the decrease as a relative-entropy sum.
The inequality `log x ≤ x - 1` bounds each positive-support term below
by joint mass minus product mass. Edge pairs have zero joint mass, so
their product mass contributes to the gap. Zero marginals are treated
explicitly. Divide by `log 2` to obtain the inequality in bits.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown: Bonnet–Chang, proof of Lemma 12, equations (17) and (18).

proofs.description:
Every enumerated sublist has no duplicates and length `k`. Conversely, filter
the vertex list by the desired finite set to obtain its unique ordered sublist.

The length of prescribed-size sublists is the binomial coefficient, which
is at most the corresponding power of the list length.

The first successful candidate is an independent set of size `k`. If an
independent set had size at least `k` after failure, selecting a size-`k`
subset would give a successful candidate, a contradiction.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown: Bonnet–Chang, exhaustive-search rejection in Lemma 14.

proofs.description:
Split assignments into the selected coordinates and their complement.
Sum the complement product to one, then reindex selected coordinates
by the given embedding.

Expand the sum over all assignments into a product of coordinate sums.
Every coordinate has mass one.

Apply the proved split certificate dichotomy. A high-value flow would
produce a uniform-endpoint route distribution. Its load bound and the
scale inequality give loads at most ell*x/k, contradicting the proved
sparse-route obstruction. The remaining branch gives exactly the projected
cut shores and separator cost bound.

The expected entropy drop exceeds 2/p. Choices below the probability
floor contribute at most 1/(2p), using the parent entropy bound. If every
remaining choice dropped by at most 1/p, the total drop would be at most

selected entropy with that of the enlarged conditioning set.

Induct through heavy entropy-decreasing choices, retaining raw moment

by k times its marginal probability, hence by at least tau since k≥1.
If every admissible set above the final moment floor remained expensive,
r steps would force negative entropy. Conditioning invariants supply
the bounded costs and exact mass of the resulting sparse set.

Cast the exact rational threshold and cleared edge test to their real

it in the enumerated list. The first successful candidate retains both

Choose a Fin labeling of the route union. Map vertices inside it to their
labels and all other vertices to a fixed label. Every route lies inside
the union, so this map preserves its cardinality, connectivity, endpoints,
and induced noninteraction. The labeling is a graph isomorphism onto the
induced host and therefore preserves the unordered edge count.

The exact hull is nonempty if and only if there is an independent set
of the target cardinality.

A convex hull is nonempty precisely when its generating set is nonempty.
Unfolding the generating set gives the claimed independent set.
